# Zicy

> Zicy is an AI visibility platform for businesses without an AEO specialist, that measures how AI describes a brand, diagnoses what is inaccurate, acts on the fixes a brand controls, and proves the work moved demand, across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Google AI Mode.

## Zicy, be the brand AI gets right

https://www.zicy.com/

Be the brand AI gets right.

Customers ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI about businesses like yours every day. Zicy shows you what they hear, what to fix, and helps you fix it. No specialist required.

ChatGPT · Gemini · Perplexity · Google AI Overviews · Google AI Mode — coverage across the five engines that decide the answer.

### 01 · The shift

Ranking on Google no longer means being seen.

Search has changed. When someone asks AI about your category, the engine builds one answer before the buyer ever clicks. If your brand isn't in that answer, or isn't in it accurately, the decision gets made without you.

- **45%** — of consumers now use AI tools for local business recommendations, up from 6% a year earlier. Source: BrightLocal, n=1,002, 2026
- **51%** — of B2B software buyers now start research with AI chatbots more often than Google. Source: G2, n=1,076, 2026
- **8% vs 15%** — how often Google users click a result when an AI summary appears, versus when it doesn't. Source: Pew Research Center, 68,879 searches, 2025

And SEO is not AI visibility: just 12% of AI citations overlap with a brand's Google top-10 results. (Ahrefs, 15,000 prompts, 2025)

"The demand didn't disappear. The click did. And the answer names three businesses, not ten links."

One loop: measure, diagnose, act, prove.

### FAQ

**Q: What is AI visibility?**
AI visibility is how often, how accurately and how prominently your brand appears when people ask AI assistants about your category. It is the AI-era equivalent of search ranking, measured inside the answer the engine builds rather than in a list of links. Zicy measures it across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

**Q: Which engines does Zicy track?**
Zicy tracks the five engines that decide most answers: ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode. Enterprise plans can add others, such as Grok and DeepSeek. Every tracked prompt runs across each engine, so one prompt returns a reading from all five.

**Q: How is Zicy different from a rank tracker or a mention monitor?**
Most tools tell you whether your brand was named. Zicy also tells you whether what AI said was true, why it said it, and how to fix it, then connects the fix to demand. That is the full loop (measure, diagnose, act, prove) in one place, rather than a dashboard that stops at the scoreboard.

**Q: Does Zicy place media or write content for me?**
Zicy measures, diagnoses and gives you the tools to fix what is in your control: schema, llms.txt and content. It does not place earned media; your team earns that on its merits, and Zicy shows whether it moved the answer. For a fully managed programme, Growth.pro, the consultancy that built Zicy, runs done-for-you engagements.

**Q: Is improving AI visibility safe under Google's spam policies?**
Yes. Zicy's content tooling is built to current AEO/GEO best practice and aligned with Google's latest spam policies, updated in May 2026 to cover AI Overviews and AI Mode. The approach is to make genuine expertise easier for AI to find, verify and trust, not to game the system.

**Q: How much does Zicy cost?**
Zicy starts at $79 per month on Starter, with Growth at $199, Scale at $449, and custom Enterprise plans. Starter and Growth include a 7-day free trial, and the annual plan gives you 13 months for the price of 12.

**Q: Who is Zicy for?**
Zicy is built for five groups who own the answer: small and mid-sized businesses, brands, PR and communications teams, marketing and creative agencies, and publishers. Each gets a tailored view of the same underlying platform. See the solutions section above, or Zicy for small businesses if you run the business yourself.

An agency story, scaled into AI.

Agencies maximised their retainers while the clients stayed invisible online.

So instead of building more human-heavy agency layers, Alvin and his team cloned Growth.pro's ethos (empathy, trust, accountability, transparency and integrity) into AI itself. ## AI Citation Enablement (AICE), Growth.pro's citation practice

https://www.zicy.com/about/ai-citation-enablement

AI Citation Enablement (AICE) is Growth.pro's practice of making a brand's content and entity data easy for AI engines to find, trust, and cite as a source in their answers.

### 01 · Why it matters

Being mentioned is not being cited.

A citation attributes and links a brand as a source. It is the durable unit of AI visibility, the part that still carries value as referral clicks fall, and it is what a brand can defend and license later.

Most brands are technically hard to cite regardless of how good their content is: a weak entity definition, no llms.txt, content AI cannot retrieve, or no external corroboration. AI Citation Enablement is the practice that closes that gap, across find, trust and cite.

It is one of Growth.pro's frameworks, operationalised by Zicy. See documented outcomes on our case studies.

### 02 · How it works

Four functions, one outcome: easy to cite.

- **01 Make entities citable** — The brand's core facts, what it does, who it serves, what makes it different, must be machine-readable, consistent, and structured in formats AI systems ingest. Schema markup, llms.txt, and entity-level consistency are the starting point.
- **02 Engineer source trails** — AI engines cite sources they have ingested and trust. AICE identifies the gap between what the brand publishes and what AI actually retrieves, then closes it, through content that matches answer-intent queries and through structured citations that give AI a clear trail back to the brand.
- **03 Improve retrievability** — Content must be formatted, structured, and hosted in ways that make it easy for AI crawlers to retrieve, parse, and index. This overlaps with technical AEO: page speed, crawlability, clean HTML, structured data.
- **04 Strengthen citation-worthiness** — AI engines weight content from sources they perceive as authoritative and corroborated. AICE builds the external signal set, third-party mentions, earned media, directory presence, partner citations, that makes a brand a safer source for an AI to cite.

### 03 · How Zicy operationalises it

The practice, in the platform.

- **See it — Citation Analysis.** Shows the owned, earned, competitor and uncited breakdown, and identifies which sources AI currently cites instead of the brand.
- **Make it citable — Action Center.** The schema generator and llms.txt builder, so the brand entity is machine-readable and retrievable.
- **Earn citations — Content Generator.** Creates citation-worthy, answer-intent content grounded in genuine expertise.
- **Upgrade what exists — Content Optimizer.** Upgrades existing content to current AEO and GEO best practice.

### 04 · How Growth.pro applies it

The source engineering, run for you.

Growth.pro applies the full AICE practice in done-for-you programmes, including source-trail engineering, earned-citation strategy, and authority-building that goes beyond what a self-serve platform can execute. The Zicy platform handles the technical and content layer.

### FAQ

**Q: What is AI Citation Enablement?**
AI Citation Enablement (AICE) is Growth.pro's practice of making a brand's content and entity data structured, credible, and retrievable enough that AI engines cite the brand as a source in their answers, not just mention it, but actively credit it.

**Q: What is the difference between being mentioned and being cited in AI?**
A mention means the AI named your brand in its answer. A citation means the AI linked to your website or credited your content as a source. AICE targets citations specifically because cited brands carry more authority in AI answers and receive more referral traffic from AI platforms.

**Q: Who created AI Citation Enablement?**
AI Citation Enablement is a Growth.pro practice. Zicy operationalises its core technical and content components in the platform's Citation Analysis, Action Center, and content tooling modules.

**Q: How does AI Citation Enablement relate to traditional link building?**
Traditional link building targets search-engine crawlers and PageRank. AI Citation Enablement targets the sources, formats, and authority signals that AI engines use when deciding which brands and URLs to cite in generated answers. The mechanisms overlap in some areas (third-party credibility matters in both), but the optimisation targets are different.

**Q: Can I do AI Citation Enablement with Zicy alone?**
Zicy's platform handles the technical layer: schema, llms.txt, citation analysis, and content optimisation. The earned-citation and source-trail engineering that AICE requires at scale, placing the brand in the right external sources, is the work Growth.pro's done-for-you programmes are built to execute.

### Make your brand easy to cite

See where AI cites you, and where it paraphrases you without credit, across all five engines.

## The AI Visibility Operating System, Growth.pro's operating model

https://www.zicy.com/about/ai-visibility-operating-system

The AI Visibility Operating System is Growth.pro's full operating model for building, measuring, and sustaining a brand's presence in AI-generated answers, structured across five pillars: Strategy, Measurement, Execution, Reporting, and Governance.

### 01 · Why it matters

AI visibility is an operation, not a project.

AI visibility has no finish line. The engines update, competitors move, and a position you won last quarter can quietly erode. A campaign with an end date cannot hold ground that keeps shifting.

An operating system treats it as an ongoing programme: a strategy to aim the work, a measurement layer to read it, execution to move it, reporting to prove it, and governance to keep it consistent. The strategy pillar is where the PAVA Framework diagnostics feed in.

It is one of Growth.pro's frameworks, operationalised by Zicy. See documented outcomes on our case studies.

### 02 · How it works

Five pillars, run as one.

- **01 Strategy** — Defining the brand's AI visibility objectives, the query set that matters, the engines to prioritise, and the competitive baseline. Where PAVA diagnostics feed in.
- **02 Measurement** — Systematic tracking of mention coverage, citation rate, share of voice, average AI ranking, and AI Reality Score across the tracked prompt set and all five engines. This is the pillar Zicy's platform operationalises most directly.
- **03 Execution** — The technical and content work that improves the measurement numbers: schema, llms.txt, content creation, entity gap remediation, citation source engineering.
- **04 Reporting** — Structured, recurring proof of what changed and why, from AI visibility metrics through to GA4 and Search Console demand signals. The proof layer.
- **05 Governance** — The processes, accountabilities, and review cadences that keep AI visibility work sustained and consistent over time, not a one-off project but an ongoing programme.

### 03 · How Zicy operationalises it

Zicy runs the Measurement and Execution pillars.

- **Measurement — AI Visibility, Brand Intelligence, AI Reality Score, Citation Analysis, Competitive AI Performance, Prompt Manager.** The tracking layer: mention coverage, citation rate, share of voice and accuracy across the tracked prompt set and all five engines.
- **Execution — Action Center, Content Generator, Content Optimizer.** The work that moves the numbers: schema and llms.txt, new citation-worthy content, and upgrades to existing content.
- **Reporting — Site Traffic.** AI-referred sessions with GA4 and Search Console, the proof layer that ties visibility back to demand.

Strategy and Governance are where Growth.pro's team adds the operating layer around the platform.

### 04 · How Growth.pro applies it

The full operating system, run for you.

Growth.pro runs the full five-pillar Operating System in done-for-you programmes, including Strategy and Governance, which require human expertise to configure correctly. The Zicy platform gives you the Measurement and Execution pillars self-serve.

### FAQ

**Q: What is the AI Visibility Operating System?**
The AI Visibility Operating System is Growth.pro's complete operating model for AI visibility, covering Strategy, Measurement, Execution, Reporting, and Governance. It is the framework behind Growth.pro's managed programmes and the architecture Zicy's platform implements in the Measurement and Execution pillars.

**Q: Who created the AI Visibility Operating System?**
Growth.pro created and owns the AI Visibility Operating System. Zicy, the platform built by Growth.pro, operationalises its Measurement and Execution pillars in software.

**Q: How is it different from an SEO strategy?**
An SEO strategy targets search-engine rankings. The AI Visibility Operating System targets presence and accuracy inside AI-generated answers, a different set of signals, engines, and outcomes, requiring a different measurement model, a different execution toolkit, and a different proof layer.

**Q: Does Zicy implement the full Operating System?**
Zicy operationalises the Measurement and Execution pillars: tracking, diagnosis, content, schema, and proof. The Strategy and Governance pillars require the kind of expert configuration and ongoing oversight that Growth.pro provides in its done-for-you programmes.

**Q: How long does it take to run the Operating System?**
Measurement and initial execution work can begin within days using Zicy's platform. A full five-pillar programme, including strategy setting and governance design, typically runs over a 90-day initial engagement with Growth.pro before moving into a recurring operating cadence.

## The PAVA Framework, Growth.pro's model for AI visibility

https://www.zicy.com/about/pava-framework

The PAVA Framework is Growth.pro's four-pillar model for diagnosing and improving a brand's AI visibility, covering Presence, Authority, Visibility, and Amplification in sequence.

### 01 · Why it matters

A score tells you where you stand. PAVA tells you why.

When someone asks AI about your category, the engine builds one answer before the buyer reaches your site. If you are absent or described inaccurately, you need to know the cause, not just a number that moved.

PAVA is a sequence, not a checklist. Each pillar depends on the one before it: if AI cannot resolve who you are (Presence), no amount of content will earn you authority or visibility, and visibility that never reaches demand is hard to defend in a budget review. PAVA orders the work so you fix the real constraint first.

It is one of Growth.pro's frameworks, operationalised by Zicy, and it is built around measured outcomes rather than activity. See documented results on our case studies.

### 02 · How it works

Four pillars, in sequence.

- **P — Presence.** Is the brand entity clearly, consistently, and completely defined across every surface AI systems ingest? Gaps here mean AI cannot resolve the brand as a single coherent entity. **Fixes:** Entity schema, llms.txt, NAP consistency, social handle standardisation.
- **A — Authority.** Is the brand trusted and corroborated by independent third-party sources? AI systems weight entities that appear across multiple credible, non-self-referential sources. **Fixes:** Earned media, partner mentions, citations, third-party directory listings, founder profiles.
- **V — Visibility.** Does the brand appear in AI answers for the category queries its buyers actually ask? This is the measurement pillar: tracked prompts, mention coverage, share of voice, average AI ranking. **Fixes:** Content aligned to answer-intent queries, topical authority, citation-worthy source trails.
- **A — Amplification.** Does AI visibility translate to real demand? The proof pillar: AI-referred sessions, branded-search lift, answer-intent queries, and the correlation between winning AI answers and downstream commercial outcomes.

### 03 · How Zicy operationalises it

Each pillar maps to the platform.

- **Presence — Action Center.** The schema generator and llms.txt builder, so the brand entity is machine-readable and consistent across the surfaces AI reads.
- **Authority — Citation Analysis + Content Generator.** See which independent sources AI cites in the category, then produce citation-worthy content to earn more of them.
- **Visibility — AI Visibility, Brand Intelligence + Competitive AI Performance.** Mention coverage, citation rate, share of voice and average ranking across the five engines, with the AI Reality Score and your standing against named rivals.
- **Amplification — Site Traffic.** AI-referred sessions from GA4 and Search Console, tying winning the answer back to demand.

### 04 · How Growth.pro applies it

The framework, run for you.

Growth.pro applies PAVA through done-for-you programmes: full diagnostic, strategy, execution and governance across all four pillars. The Zicy platform puts the measurement and action layers in your hands; the managed service runs the whole sequence for teams that want the work done for them.

### FAQ

**Q: What does PAVA stand for?**
PAVA stands for Presence, Authority, Visibility, and Amplification, the four sequential pillars of the framework Growth.pro uses to diagnose and improve a brand's AI visibility.

**Q: Who created the PAVA Framework?**
Growth.pro created the PAVA Framework. It is the strategic and diagnostic model behind Growth.pro's AI visibility consultancy and managed-service programmes. Zicy, the platform built by Growth.pro, operationalises PAVA in software.

**Q: How is PAVA different from a standard SEO audit?**
A standard SEO audit measures search-engine signals such as backlinks, page speed, and keyword rankings. PAVA measures the four signals that determine AI answer-engine visibility: whether the entity is clearly defined, whether it is independently corroborated, whether it appears in AI answers for buyer queries, and whether that visibility moves demand.

**Q: Can I use the PAVA Framework without Growth.pro?**
Zicy's platform operationalises the measurement and action layers of PAVA as a self-serve tool. For a fully managed PAVA programme across all four pillars, Growth.pro runs done-for-you engagements for enterprise brands.

**Q: Where does the AI Reality Score fit in the PAVA Framework?**
The AI Reality Score sits inside the Visibility pillar, it measures not just whether a brand appears in AI answers, but whether those answers describe the brand accurately. A high mention rate with a low AI Reality Score signals a Visibility problem of a specific kind: presence without accuracy.

### Put PAVA to work on your brand

Diagnose Presence, Authority, Visibility and Amplification across all five engines.

## How a Malaysian Aesthetic Clinic Group Turned AI Visibility Into 221 Tracked Purchases, Up 256.45%

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/aesthetic-clinic-ai-referred-purchases

Search visibility used to be one number stack: rankings, clicks, sessions. AI added a second stack most brands still cannot see: mentions, citations, share of voice, sentiment, and position, measured at the level of an individual question a real buyer asks.

The client is a Malaysian aesthetic clinic group in a B2C, high-consideration, heavily researched category, exactly where someone opens ChatGPT and asks which clinic is best for a specific concern before they ever open Google. This engagement measured both the visibility side and the revenue side of the same funnel.

### What we did

- **Tracked real patient-intent prompts, not keywords:** treatment queries, concern queries, clinic-selection queries, across five AI engines.
- **Made the clinic extractable:** treatment content restructured so an engine can lift a clean, quotable answer.
- **Used the gaps as the content roadmap:** weak-coverage prompts became the priority list, strong-coverage prompts got reinforced before competitors moved in.
- **Watched the competitive set, not just the client:** mentions, citations, ranking, and share of voice benchmarked against the top five competing clinics, monthly.
- **Connected it to the money:** referral traffic from ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Copilot, tracked through to engagement and purchases.

### The visibility numbers

- **Mention coverage: 39.01%** (815 of 2,089 AI responses mentioned the brand)
- **Web citation rate: 36.24%** (757 responses linked to the site)
- **Share of voice: 16.44%** (3,227 of 19,626 total brand mentions in the category)
- **Average AI ranking: #2.54**
- **Sentiment: 78/100 positive**

Over two months, share of voice moved from 12.2% to 16.4%, brand mentions from 920 to 2,307, and average ranking from 3.0 to 2.5.

### Category leadership, with a number attached

Share of voice on its own is a vanity metric. Share of voice next to competitors is a market position. This clinic held 16.44% share of voice against 6.07% for the next best competitor, then 5.77%, 4.71%, 3.92%, and 3.60%. Nearly three times the nearest rival, in a category with five actively visible competitors, while sentiment held at 78/100, the highest in the set.

At prompt level the strength was distributed, not propped up by one or two queries. Multiple prompts held 3/5 or 4/5 platform coverage, individual prompts reached 41.67% share of voice, and average positions clustered between #1 and #2 on the queries that matter most.

### From visibility to revenue

Visibility is the leading indicator. This is the lagging one, measured year on year over seven months:

- 13,225 sessions from ChatGPT alone, against 4,138 a year earlier: up 219.6%
- 10,767 engaged sessions, up 170.9%
- 221 purchases, against 62: up 256.45%
- Gemini referrals up 1,048%, Perplexity up 150%, Copilot from zero

Purchases grew faster than the traffic that produced them. The standard objection to AI referral traffic is that it is curious browsers, high volume and low intent. Here the opposite happened: someone who arrives already told by an AI that this clinic is a credible option arrives further down the funnel than someone who clicked a blue link.

One honest caveat: the visibility window is two months, while the traffic comparison is seven months year on year. They are not the same period, and this is not a claim that one caused the other in a straight line.

### The takeaway

Nearly all of this clinic's converting traffic came from ChatGPT, the one engine where its visibility was weakest at 15.9% coverage. Perplexity, at 63.1% coverage, sent 120 sessions. ChatGPT, at 15.9%, sent 13,225. Coverage and revenue are not the same axis, and averaging them into a single visibility score hides exactly the thing a brand needs to see. The strategy question is no longer how to get mentioned more. It is: which engine do buyers actually use, and what is the brand's position there specifically.

## How an Aesthetic Clinic Drove 52% Mentions, 29.75% Citations & Increased AI Share of Voice from 5.4% to 9.4%

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/aesthetic-clinic-ai-visibility

In the aesthetic industry, discovery increasingly begins inside AI answers, and not search result pages.

When prospective patients ask AI platforms about treatments, safety, comparisons, or suitability, the brands that appear in those responses shape perception long before a website visit.

This aesthetic clinic wanted to understand a simple but critical question: how often is our brand actually being surfaced in AI answers, and how is that changing over time?

**AI Visibility & Authority Metrics**

- **Brand Mention Coverage: 52%**
- **Website Citation Coverage: 29.75%**
- **Average AI Ranking: 1.89** across 135 tracked prompts
- **Share of Voice: 9.33%** overall

**2-Month Performance Trend**

- **Share of Voice increased from 5.4% → 9.4%**
- **Brand Mentions grew from 117 → 1,046**

### What Was Done (Strategy Breakdown)

**1. AI Visibility Baseline & Gap Identification**

- Measured brand mentions, citations, and rankings across 400 tracked AI responses.
- Identified prompts where competitors were referenced more frequently.
- Prioritised treatment-related prompts with commercial intent.

**2. Treatment-Level AEO Optimisation**

- Refined treatment pages to improve clarity around suitability, benefits vs alternatives, and safety considerations.
- Structured content in answer-ready formats, preferred by AI systems.

**3. Authority & Trust Reinforcement**

- Strengthened brand-procedure associations.
- Reduced ambiguous phrasing that can cause AI systems to default to neutral or larger competitors.
- Improved contextual cues AI models rely on for citation confidence.

**4. Continuous Tracking & Iteration**

- Monitored changes in share of voice and brand mentions weekly.
- Validated improvements through ranking and citation movement, not assumptions.
- Adjusted optimisation focus based on prompt-level performance.

### Why Tracking AI Visibility Matters for Aesthetic Clinics

AI systems increasingly influence early treatment consideration. Visibility loss doesn't always show up in search rankings. Patients often form perceptions before visiting a clinic's website.

Without measurement, clinics don't know which procedures AI associates with their brand, and competitor visibility gaps remain hidden. With tracking, share of voice becomes measurable, improvements can be validated over time, and strategy shifts from reactive to data-led.

### What This Case Study Signals

This clinic did not chase traffic alone. They focused on understanding how AI systems interpret credibility, treatment relevance, and brand authority.

As healthcare and aesthetic discovery increasingly shifts toward AI-generated answers, visibility is not about being searchable, but about being referenced and recommended.

Platforms like Zicy make this visibility measurable, enabling brands to adapt as AI-driven discovery continues to evolve.

## From Zero to 99 AI Citations: How This Brand Captured 12,800% More Traffic

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/architectural-services-ai-citations

In today's AI-first search landscape, the biggest win isn't ranking on page one, it's becoming the source AI platforms cite.

That's exactly the transformation we engineered for a client in architectural services. Starting with zero AI mentions, they quickly built a reputation as a trusted authority across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Copilot, all without a single paid ad.

The project began in December 2024 with one clear goal: turn the brand into an answer, not just a search result.

### The Results (as of August 2025)

**AI Citations Secured: 99**

- **ChatGPT**: 41 citations on 12 pages (+39 vs baseline)
- **Google AI Overviews**: 20 citations on 17 pages (+19)
- **Gemini**: 16 citations on 15 pages (+14)
- **Perplexity**: 15 citations on 7 pages (+13)
- **Copilot**: 7 citations on 3 pages (+5)

**AI Traffic Performance**

- **Total AI-sourced users**: 278
- **New AI users**: 235
- **Year-on-year AI traffic growth**: +12,800%
- **Year-on-year AI events growth**: +21,800%
- **Key events from AI users**: 29

**Branded vs Non-Branded Impact**

Branded queries saw steady growth. Non-branded queries surged, confirming stronger discovery via AI-driven responses.

### The Strategy Behind the Growth

**1. Restructuring for AI Discovery**

- Expanded content into long-form Q&A formats designed for snippet extraction.
- Deployed schema.org markup including FAQ, How-To, and Author schemas.

**2. Entity Optimisation for Generative Engines**

- Strengthened topical authority by mapping content to Google's Knowledge Graph entities.
- Improved brand mention consistency to align with AI Overviews inclusion criteria.
- Built internal linking structures to clarify entity relationships across the site.

**3. Monitoring & Testing Across AI Platforms**

- Tracked presence inside Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT responses, Gemini, Perplexity, and Copilot.
- Conducted iterative Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO) testing to refine visibility triggers.

**4. Zero-Click AI Traffic Tracking**

- Designed a custom analytics dashboard to separate AI-generated answer referrals from AI-driven search traffic.
- Monitored the citations to sessions to conversions pipeline for attribution clarity.

### Key Takeaway

Ranking on Google is no longer the endgame. In an era where AI answers shape buying journeys, being cited directly inside these responses is what drives discovery.

This client's journey proves that with the right AEO + GEO framework, even a brand starting from zero can achieve authority inside AI ecosystems, translating into visibility, traffic, and meaningful conversions.

## How a B2B Logistics Manufacturer Reached 67.4% AI Mention Coverage and 65.57% Citation Coverage Across Five Platforms

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/b2b-logistics-ai-procurement-filter

There is a moment in every B2B purchase that most marketing teams never see. A procurement engineer, a compliance officer, or a technical buyer asks an AI assistant to explain a standard, compare an option, or name who does this properly, before an RFQ, a vendor shortlist, or a single phone call.

This client operates in the certified offshore container space, where compliance language is the buying criteria. Strong engineering, real certifications, genuine category expertise. And almost no presence in the AI answers where that expertise was being asked about.

In certification-driven industries, being left out of an AI answer does not just cost a sale. It costs technical legitimacy. Buyers were not asking AI for recommendations. They were asking it to validate standards: DNV 2.7-1, EN 12079, load testing, certification scope.

### What we did

We treated this as four separate problems, not one.

- **Prompt-level visibility mapping.** We mapped 140+ high-intent prompts a real buyer actually asks, decision-stage, specification-heavy, compliance-led, rather than generic keywords.
- **Certification-focused entity strengthening.** We made the brand unambiguously legible to machines on the standards it actually owns, with pages structured so an AI can extract a clean, quotable, citable answer.
- **Share of voice expansion.** We tracked competitor density inside certification clusters and reinforced the prompts where rivals were gaining ground, before they consolidated.
- **Citation consistency.** We worked the formatting, structure, and source authority until the brand's own site became the thing AI links to, not just the thing it paraphrases.

### The results

Across five AI platforms:

- **Brand mention coverage: 67.4%** (184 of 273 responses), up 41.3% on the prior period
- **Website citation coverage: 65.57%**, up 22.3%
- **Share of voice: 23.73%** (931 of 3,712 total brand mentions), up 57.7%
- **Average AI ranking: #2.64**

**By platform:** Google AI Overviews 93.9%, Perplexity 92.9%, Google AI Mode 91.1%, Gemini 44.6%, ChatGPT 17.9%.

At topic level, the brand registered as a Brand Leader across 419 topics, with 70 to 87% coverage in its core certification territory: 72% on DNV 2.7-1 / EN 12079, 87% on DNV 2.7-1 / ISO 10855. Of 1,895 topics detected, 419 are ones where the brand leads, 19 are contested battlegrounds, and 1,457 are blind spots.

### The takeaway

The engines do not think alike. They weight different sources, trust different signals, and reward different structures. This brand is near-dominant in Google's ecosystem and still building in ChatGPT's, and that gap is quantified, not vague. A named gap with a known size, on the platform with the largest assistant user base, is not a weakness in the report. It is next quarter's roadmap.

AI visibility is a measurable position, not a vibe. It can be known, tracked, attacked, defended, and lost, the same way market share can.

## How One eCommerce Brand Boosted Visibility With 531 More AI Citations in 4 Months

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/ecommerce-531-ai-citations

What if product discovery no longer begins with Google, but with ChatGPT?

Today's consumers are skipping search engines and going straight to conversational platforms, asking questions like "which is the best product for X?" or "what's a good alternative to Y?"

That shift opened a new frontier for an eCommerce brand. We realised that to win online, they had to become the answer itself, not just appear near it.

Through a focused AI visibility strategy, we went beyond traditional SEO. We restructured content to be cited by platforms like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini, and saw a measurable lift in both visibility and conversions.

### The results, within 4 months

**AI Platform Citations Skyrocketed**

Their brand began appearing as a go-to recommendation across multiple generative AI tools:

- **Google AI Overviews**: 225 citations (up 168), spread over 67 pages
- **ChatGPT**: 117 citations (up 118), across 67 pages
- **Perplexity**: 81 citations (up 78), across 53 pages
- **Gemini**: 71 citations (up 65), across 69 pages
- **Copilot (Microsoft)**: 37 citations (up 32), across 27 pages

**Share of Voice: Beating the Competition on ChatGPT**

Brand visibility wasn't just rising, it was dominating: their brand secured 53.6% of ChatGPT brand mentions, while the top competitor trailed with only 24.2% share.

### Strategy Breakdown

**1. AI Citation Engineering**

Instead of chasing backlinks, the team engineered content that AI models want to cite: structured brand anchors using entity-based markup, answer-driven paragraphs with clear contextual framing, and external linking styled for AI interpretation and traceability.

**2. Multimodal Content Upgrades**

They went beyond text: product pages enhanced with image alt text and visual schema, plus infographics and short-form videos to support AI's multimodal outputs.

**3. AEO + Intent-First Content Structure**

Rather than focusing on keywords, they wrote content that answers questions: sections answering "which is best for…", "should I choose…", "difference between…", long-tail semantic triggers and layered FAQ schemas, and headers crafted for maximum contextual clarity.

**4. AI Traffic Monitoring Across Platforms**

Referrer tracking and analytics integration allowed them to track ChatGPT user flow via chat.openai.com, and Perplexity and Gemini origin traffic.

### The takeaway

While others are still optimising for search rankings, this brand bet on a different game: be the source AI platforms trust and recommend, and make your product the answer.

That shift in strategy paid off, in both visibility and bottom-line growth.

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/ecommerce-ai-ready-content

The outcome? Not incremental change, but a step-level jump in performance.

- **Monthly clicks** surged 290.32%, climbing from 1.55K to 6.05K
- **Monthly impressions** grew 457.14%, from 105K to 585K
- **Average search position** improved by 15 spots, from 31.1 to 16.1

**2. Layered Content Enhancements**

Instead of adding volume, we enriched key pages with FAQs tuned for buyer questions, short trust-building snippets, and contextual details that improved semantic depth.

**3. Intelligent Internal Linking**

AI-guided mapping connected product pages, parent categories, and blogs into a logical content web, amplifying crawl efficiency and signalling stronger relevance to search engines.

**4. Continuous Optimisation Loop**

Every 30 days, we applied micro-adjustments informed by weekly AI performance tracking, ensuring content evolved with user behaviour and SERP shifts.

**5. Entity-Level Authority Signals**

We embedded structured metadata and NLP-driven entity optimisation so that search engines could better associate the brand with topical authority in its product niches.

### The big lesson

This case study wasn't about writing more. It was about writing smarter. AI became the lens through which we refined strategy: surfacing content gaps, aligning with buyer intent, and structuring pages so they were easy for both users and algorithms to understand.

The takeaway? Brands that combine human strategy with AI precision don't just compete in search, they leap ahead. If your pages aren't yet AI-optimised, your competitors may already be one step closer to capturing your audience.

## AI Traffic That Converts: 785 ChatGPT Users Driving 1,816 Events (+406%)

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/ecommerce-ai-referred-traffic

What if your future customers never Google you, yet still find you?

That's the new reality of discovery. Platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity are increasingly where people ask their most urgent questions, and where buying decisions quietly begin.

For our client, the challenge was clear: could they harness these AI-driven moments to generate real users and measurable conversions? The answer: absolutely.

By aligning content, structure, and tracking for AI-first discoverability, this brand turned experimental AI traffic into a consistent growth engine.

### The results

Between January – July 2025, the client saw clear growth across AI platforms:

- **785 users from ChatGPT**, marking a 288.5% increase
- **149 users from Perplexity.ai**, with 26.0% growth
- **69 users from Gemini (Google)**, showing 19.9% growth
- **45 users from Perplexity**, up 9.8%
- **21 users from Edge (Bing AI)**, delivering a 52.4% increase
- **19 users from Copilot (Microsoft)**, with 19.5% growth

And the most important metric, conversion-driving activity: 1,966 tracked key events (from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Perplexity.ai, Edge, Copilot), with a 406.4% jump in key events from ChatGPT alone. Significant event growth also came from Gemini (+42.7%), Perplexity (+51.7%), Edge (+54.7%) and Copilot (+36.8%).

### How we did it

**1. Rethinking Research**

Instead of starting with keywords, the team pinpointed customer pain points and USP-led messaging, built topic clusters around high-intent themes, analysed competitor mentions inside AI responses rather than just SERPs, and focused efforts on bottom-funnel content to drive leads, not vanity clicks.

**2. Making Content AI-Readable**

To increase the chance of being cited and surfaced: added concise takeaway sections for snippet-style answers, structured content in an "answer-first" inverted pyramid style, and embedded FAQ blocks addressing common questions.

**3. Technical SEO With AI in Mind**

Optimisations ensured AI models could easily interpret content: schema markup rolled out across all product/service pages, fixed header hierarchies (H1–H6) for logical flow, improved image alt text for clarity, and updated robots.txt to give AI crawlers full access to priority pages.

**4. Measuring AI Traffic Directly**

To avoid guesswork, the brand established tracking systems to isolate AI-originating traffic, behavioural analysis to map AI-driven conversion journeys, and a feedback cycle where insights shaped new content creation.

### The takeaway

AI platforms aren't just a novelty. They're a growing part of the customer journey. By adapting both content and technical infrastructure to this new search environment, the brand positioned itself not just to be found, but to be trusted and chosen.

This case study looks at how an education sector services provider used AI visibility measurement to understand where it appeared in AI-generated answers, and how that visibility translated into meaningful year-over-year traffic growth.

- **Website Citation Coverage:** 36.51%
- **Average AI Ranking:** 2.44 across tracked prompts

**Year-over-Year AI Traffic Impact (GA4):** AI-driven sessions increased by over 12,507% YoY (2024 vs. 2025). Engaged sessions grew by more than 12,845%. ChatGPT emerged as the dominant AI traffic source, with incremental growth from Perplexity and Gemini.

### What Was Done (Strategy Breakdown)

**1. AI Visibility Baseline**

- Measured brand presence across 39 real-world prompts and 5 AI platforms.
- Established benchmarks for mentions, citations, rankings, and share of voice.
- Identified where competitors were referenced instead, despite similar positioning.

- Tracked how individual prompts performed across platforms.
- Highlighted prompts with strong rankings but weak brand mentions.
- Used these gaps to prioritise optimisation efforts.

- Refined key service pages to improve attribution clarity.

**4. Continuous Measurement**

- Monitored visibility trends over time rather than relying on one-off snapshots.
- Used changes in rankings, mentions, and citations to validate progress.

### Why Tracking AI Visibility Matters for Service Brands

AI systems increasingly act as filters, not just information sources. Visibility gaps often don't show up in traditional analytics until later stages.

Without AI visibility tracking, brands don't know where they're excluded from recommendations, and competitive losses happen quietly. With tracking, visibility becomes measurable, and optimisation aligns with real discovery behaviour, not assumptions.

This organisation didn't focus on chasing rankings alone. They focused on understanding how AI systems surface, compare, and reference brands in their category. Platforms like Zicy help make this layer observable, so organisations can adapt as discovery models continue to evolve.

## How an Education Brand Reached 56.32% AI Mentions, 51.05% Citations Across 5 AI Platforms

https://www.zicy.com/case-studies/education-owned-earned-citations

If AI were asked to recommend institutions in your category today, would your brand make the shortlist?

For this education-sector client, AI visibility was inconsistent across platforms. The results show what structured AEO execution can achieve.

**AI Visibility & Authority Signals**

- **Brand Mention Coverage:** 56.32%
- **Website Citation Coverage:** 51.05%
- **Share of Voice:** 12.47%
- **Average AI Ranking:** 2.98 across tracked prompts

**Competitive Positioning (Top 5 Brands Tracked)**

Brand ranked within Top 3 positions on average, achieved 12.5% Share of Voice, outperforming competitors at 8.2%, 3.3%, 3.2%, and below, and had the highest overall citation volume among tracked brands (97 citations).

**Citation Analysis:** 149 Owned Authority citations, 529 Earned Authority citations, 197 Competitor citations monitored. This gave clarity on influence, not just mentions.

**AI Traffic Impact (GA4 – Dec 19 to Mar 18):** 218 AI-driven sessions, 109 engaged sessions, 50% engagement rate. AI traffic contributed to form submissions, WhatsApp enquiries, and multi-session engagement.

### What We Changed (Strategy)

**1. Prompt-Level Visibility Mapping**

- Tracked 38 high-conversion-intent prompts across 5 major AI platforms.
- Identified specific gaps in mention density and citation frequency.
- Prioritised prompts that signalled strong commercial intent from prospective students.

**2. Entity Strengthening & Structured Authority**

Reinforced institutional positioning by implementing clear definitional statements to help AI categorise the brand accurately, program-specific structured sections for better indexing and retrieval, and FAQ blocks specifically aligned with AI extractability requirements.

**3. Citation Ecosystem Expansion**

- Analysed the balance between "Earned Authority" (third-party mentions) vs "Owned Authority" (brand-controlled content).
- Strengthened the technical authority of pages most likely to be used as primary citations by LLMs.

**4. Share of Voice Optimisation**

- Identified specific query clusters where competitors were appearing more frequently.
- Optimised content for comparison-style queries (e.g., "Brand A vs Brand B").
- Improved contextual relevance to ensure inclusion inside multi-brand AI recommendations.

**5. AI Traffic Measurement**

- Connected AI brand mentions to actual website sessions and engagement metrics.
- Measured event triggers such as form submissions and WhatsApp inquiries.
- Shifted from "visibility vanity" to focusing on measurable student intent.

### Why Tracking AI Visibility Matters

Education is a high-consideration journey. When AI answers specific student queries such as "best institutions for X program", "top colleges for Y field", or "where to study Z in [location]", the brand that appears repeatedly becomes the default recommendation.

The risks of staying "blind" to AI: zero awareness of whether your brand is even being mentioned in AI-driven searches, citation loss to whoever is being cited as the authority instead of you, influence gaps in identifying which specific prompts are driving market influence, and competitive risk in being unable to defend your brand against competitors actively shaping AI narratives.

Winning here is not about writing longer blogs; it's about structured, extractable authority. If your institution has a visibility gap, it is measurable, and once it's measurable, it's optimisable.

## Cookie policy, Zicy

https://www.zicy.com/legal/cookies

Legal

Cookie policy

Last updated: 6 August 2026 · Effective: 6 August 2026

This policy explains the cookies and similar technologies Zicy uses, what each one is for, and how to change your choices. It sits alongside our privacy policy. It covers both www.zicy.com and app.zicy.com: Google and Stripe set some cookies at the shared .zicy.com domain, so a visitor cannot tell which host set what.

Privacy policy · Cookie settings

### 1. The short version

- Cookies that keep you signed in and keep the service secure are always on. The site cannot work without them.
- Everything else is off until you say yes.
- You can change your mind at any time using Cookie settings in the footer.
- We do not use cookies to sell your data or to build advertising profiles about you.

### 2. What a cookie is

A cookie is a small text file a website stores on your device so it can recognise your browser on a later visit.

We use the word cookie loosely in this policy to also cover similar technologies, which do a comparable job:

- **Local storage and session storage,** which hold data in your browser rather than in a cookie file.
- **Pixels and tags,** small pieces of code that record that a page or an email was opened.
- **Software development kits,** code inside our Chrome extension and WordPress plugin.

The marketing site at www.zicy.com is served as static files, with no request-time server, so it cannot set cookies itself. Every storage item you can find on either www.zicy.com or app.zicy.com is set by client-side code, or by the Zicy app's own sign-in and payment systems, and is listed in section 4.

### 3. The categories we use

**Strictly necessary.** These are required for the service to function and are set without consent, because you cannot use Zicy without them. They do things like keep you signed in across pages, remember which brand profile is active, protect forms against cross-site request forgery, balance server load, and enforce your plan's limits.

**Functional.** These remember preferences so the product behaves the way you left it. Examples are the light and dark theme toggle, your language, your dismissal of a banner, and your saved filters. Turning these off does not break Zicy, but it will keep forgetting your choices.

**Analytics.** These tell us which pages and features are used, where people get stuck, and which errors are firing. We use this to fix and improve the product. We use Google Consent Mode v2. Before you give consent, analytics runs without cookies and without personalised advertising signals.

### 4. The cookies we actually set

| Name | Provider | Category | Purpose | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| zicy-consent | Zicy, first party, browser localStorage | Strictly necessary | Stores your cookie choice so the banner does not ask again | Until you clear site data. Browser storage has no expiry date |
| currentToken | Zicy, first party | Strictly necessary | Keeps you signed in to the Zicy app | Until you sign out or the session expires |
| firebase:authUser | Google Firebase, first party, browser localStorage | Strictly necessary | Holds your sign-in session for the Zicy app | Until you sign out |
| __stripe_mid | Stripe | Strictly necessary | Fraud prevention on payment pages | 1 year |
| __stripe_sid | Stripe | Strictly necessary | Fraud prevention within a single session | 30 minutes |
| _ga | Google Analytics, first party | Analytics | Distinguishes one visitor from another | 2 years |
| _ga_YEW4D13JKT and _ga_KV5E88LTXN | Google Analytics, first party | Analytics | Keep session state for the Zicy website and the Zicy app respectively | 2 years |

The analytics cookies are set only after you accept analytics cookies. If you decline, Zicy's site measurement runs without cookies.

Cookie names and lifetimes change as we ship. If you find one on our site that is not listed here, tell us at privacy@zicy.com and we will correct this page.

### 5. Third parties that can set cookies

- **Google,** for Tag Manager, Analytics 4 and Firebase Authentication. policies.google.com/privacy
- **Stripe,** for payment processing and payment fraud prevention. stripe.com/privacy
- **Vercel,** for privacy-friendly site analytics that sets no cookies and no browser storage. vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy

Where a third party sets a cookie through our site, that provider's own notice governs what it does with the data. We choose our providers carefully and bind them by contract, but we do not control their notices.

### 6. How to change your choices

- **On our site:** open Cookie settings here or in the footer. Your choice is stored and applied on every later visit. This is Zicy's own consent tool; we do not use a third-party consent platform.
- **In your browser:** every major browser lets you block or delete cookies in its settings. Blocking strictly necessary cookies will stop Zicy from working.

Clearing your cookies also clears your stored consent choice, so you will be asked again on your next visit.

### 7. Consent, and where it applies

If you are in the European Economic Area or the United Kingdom, we ask for your consent before setting any cookie that is not strictly necessary, and we do not treat continued browsing as consent.

If you are in Malaysia, Personal Data Protection Act 2010 as amended, or in California, we still give you the same controls. We think one standard is simpler than three.

You can withdraw consent at any time, and withdrawing is as easy as giving it.

### 8. Changes to this policy

We update this page when our cookies change, and we change the date at the top. If a change means we need your consent again, we will ask.

### 9. Contact

- **Questions about cookies:** privacy@zicy.com
- **Postal address:** Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd., 60 Persiaran Midlands, 10250 Penang, Malaysia
- **More detail on how we handle personal data:** see the privacy policy

## Privacy policy, Zicy

https://www.zicy.com/legal/privacy

Legal

Privacy policy

Last updated: 6 August 2026

This policy is published in English and in Bahasa Malaysia. If this English version conflicts with the Bahasa Malaysia version, the English version prevails.

This policy explains what Zicy collects, why, who we share it with, and what you can ask us to do about it. Zicy is operated by Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd. in Penang, Malaysia.

Cookie policy · Cookie settings · Bahasa Malaysia

### 1. The short version

A plain-English summary. It is a summary only, and the rest of this policy governs.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Who runs Zicy | Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd., a company registered in Malaysia. |
| What we mainly hold | Your account details, your billing details, the brands and prompts you choose to track, and the data you connect from Google, Bing and your own website. |
| Do we sell your data | No. We do not sell personal data and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. |
| How long we keep it | While your account is active, then for the periods set out in section 12. |

### 2. Who this policy covers

This policy applies to:

- The Zicy web application at app.zicy.com
- The Zicy marketing website at zicy.com and the help centre at docs.zicy.com
- The Zicy Chrome extension
- The public AEO and GEO consultant tool at zicy.com/consultant
- The Zicy WordPress plugin
- Email, support and sales conversations with us

It does not cover third-party websites we link to, or what an AI platform does with a question you type into it directly.

### 3. When we are the controller and when we are the processor

This distinction matters if you are buying Zicy on behalf of a client or an employer.

**We are the data controller for:** your account and profile details; your organisation, team and invitation records; billing, subscription and quota records; product usage, device and log data; marketing and support communications.

**We are the data processor for:** brand profiles, tracked prompts and competitor lists you enter; analytics and Search Console data you connect; content crawled from a website you nominate; AI engine responses captured for your tracked prompts; content drafts generated or optimised in the product.

For that second group you, or the client you act for, are the controller. Our processing terms for that data are available on request from privacy@zicy.com.

### 4. What we collect and why

Everything below is either given to us by you, generated by your use of Zicy, or fetched from a service you connected.

**4.1 Account and identity.** What: full name, email address, password (stored hashed, never in readable form), organisation name, organisation ID, sign-in method, role, profile access scope. Why: to create and secure your account, apply permissions, and provide the service. Legal basis, where the GDPR applies: performance of a contract.

**4.2 Team and invitations.** What: the email address, role and status of anyone you invite, and the expiry of their invitation. Why: to run team access and quota allocation. Note: if you invite a colleague, you are asking us to email them on your behalf. Only invite people who expect to hear from you. Legal basis: performance of a contract, and our legitimate interest in operating team features.

**4.3 Billing and subscription.** What: plan, quota and credit usage, add-on purchases, voucher redemptions, invoices, billing contact details. Why: to take payment, issue invoices, meet tax and accounting obligations. Legal basis: performance of a contract, and legal obligation.

**4.4 Brand and prompt data.** What: brand names and variations, website URLs, industry, products and services, mission, unique selling proposition, tone and writing style, competitor names and URLs, brand facts such as founding year and headquarters, the prompts you track, and the tags you apply. Why: every Zicy module is calibrated against this. Without it we cannot measure anything. Personal data warning: these fields are free text. Do not enter personal data about individuals unless you need to, and never enter special category data such as health or biometric information. Legal basis: performance of a contract. Where the data belongs to your client, we process it on your instructions.

**4.5 AI engine responses.** What: the answers ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode return for your tracked prompts, plus the brands, positions, sentiment and citations we extract from them. How: we send your tracked prompt to each engine on a daily cycle and record the response. Incidental personal data: an AI answer can name a person, for example a founder or an author. We store the answer as returned so you have the evidence. Legal basis: performance of a contract, and our legitimate interest in providing a measurement record you can rely on.

**4.6 Connected Google accounts.** Covered separately in section 5, because Google imposes specific rules on us.

**4.7 Connected Bing Webmaster Tools.** What: impressions, clicks, click-through rate, average position, top pages and top queries for the property you connect. Why: Bing's index also feeds Microsoft Copilot and other answer engines, so it is part of your visibility picture. Legal basis: performance of a contract.

**4.8 WordPress plugin and AI bot logs.** What: access-log records showing which AI crawlers visited your site and which pages they read. Depending on your server configuration these logs can contain IP addresses and user-agent strings. Why: to show you which AI assistants are actually reading your site and where they take answers from. Your responsibility: you are the controller of your own server logs. Only sync them if you are entitled to. Legal basis: performance of a contract, on your instructions.

**4.9 Website crawl data.** What: page URLs, titles, meta descriptions, headings, body content, structured data, robots.txt, sitemap and llms.txt for the domain you nominate. Why: to run site audits, page summaries, duplicate detection and content scoring. Limit: we crawl only domains you nominate on a brand profile, and we never publish or change anything on your website. Every asset Zicy produces is handed to you to publish yourself. Legal basis: performance of a contract.

**4.10 Ask Zicy and the AI consultant.** What: the messages you type into Ask Zicy, the chat tab titles you set, and the responses returned. Why: to answer your question and to meter chat usage against your plan. Legal basis: performance of a contract.

**4.11 Generated and optimised content.** What: article drafts, optimised page copy, schema markup and llms.txt files produced in the product, and the inputs you gave to produce them. Why: so your content library persists and you can return to a draft. Legal basis: performance of a contract.

**4.12 Product usage, device and log data.** What: IP address, browser and device type, pages and features used, timestamps, referring URL, error and diagnostic records. Why: to keep the service secure, diagnose faults, prevent abuse, and understand which features are used. Legal basis: legitimate interests in securing and improving the service.

**4.13 Communications and marketing.** What: contact form and demo request details, support conversations, and email preferences. Why: to reply to you and to send product and marketing email you have asked for. Control: the notification centre in Settings has a master switch to pause all optional emails. Emails about payments, invoices and invitations are operational and are always sent. Legal basis: consent for marketing, legitimate interests for operational messages.

### 5. Google user data, and Google's Limited Use requirements

If you connect Google Analytics or Google Search Console, Zicy accesses Google user data through Google APIs, with your explicit permission at the consent screen.

**What we access:** Google Analytics traffic, source and engagement metrics for the property you select, including the AI referral sources we report on; Google Search Console query, impression, click, click-through rate and position data for the property you select; the email address of the connected Google account, so you can see which account is linked and disconnect it.

**How we use it:** only to produce the reports and features you can see in Zicy. Nothing else.

**The Limited Use commitment.** Zicy's use and transfer of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. In practice that means: we use Google user data only to provide or improve features that are visible and prominent in Zicy; we do not transfer Google user data except to provide those features with your consent, for security purposes, to comply with the law, or in a merger, acquisition or sale of assets; we do not allow humans to read Google user data, except where you have specifically agreed, where it is necessary for security or to comply with the law, or where the data is aggregated for internal operations; we do not use Google user data for advertising, and we do not sell it.

**How to disconnect:** open Site Traffic in the app and choose Disconnect on the Analytics or Search Console tab, or revoke Zicy's access at myaccount.google.com/permissions. Revoking access stops future syncing. To delete data already imported, contact privacy@zicy.com.

### 6. The Chrome extension

The Zicy Chrome extension audits a page for AI readiness when you ask it to.

- It analyses a page only when you trigger an audit. It does not run in the background.
- It does not track or transmit your browsing history.
- It does not sell or share your data with third parties for their own purposes.
- Uninstalling the extension stops all collection.

### 7. The public AEO and GEO consultant

The consultant tool at zicy.com/consultant is open to visitors without an account.

- We process the questions and URLs you submit in order to answer them.
- Do not paste confidential or personal information into a public tool.

### 8. How we use AI, and whether your data trains models

This is the question buyers ask most, so we answer it directly. We use AI in two different ways, and we keep them separate rather than blur them together.

**OpenAI: Ask Zicy, embeddings, content and analysis.** Ask Zicy, our embeddings, and our content and analysis tools run on OpenAI's API. OpenAI does not use API data to train its models unless the customer opts in to that. Zicy has not opted in. OpenAI may retain API inputs and outputs for up to 30 days for abuse monitoring, then deletes them. OpenAI has completed a SOC 2 Type 2 audit covering the API platform.

**Tracked prompts sent to the AI engines we measure.** Separately from how we use OpenAI, Zicy sends your tracked prompts to ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode, in order to record what those engines answer. That is the product itself.

We do use aggregated and de-identified statistics, which cannot identify you or your clients, to improve Zicy's benchmarks and features. We do not make decisions about you that have a legal or similarly significant effect using automated processing alone.

### 9. Cookies and similar technologies

We use cookies and similar technologies for sign-in and security, for remembering preferences such as the theme toggle, and for measuring how the site and product are used.

Non-essential cookies are set only with your consent, and you can change your choice at any time using Cookie settings in the footer. The full list is in the cookie policy.

### 10. Who we share data with

We share personal data only with the categories below, and only as far as needed.

- **Service providers, sometimes called sub-processors.** Hosting, database, email delivery, payments, error monitoring, product analytics and AI providers. Each is engaged under its published terms, and where a data processing agreement is in place, it requires that provider to protect the data and process it only on our instructions.
- **The AI engines we measure.** We send your tracked prompt text.
- **Your own organisation.** Anyone you invite can see the profiles they are assigned to. An owner can see the organisation's usage and billing.
- **Professional advisers, auditors and insurers,** under confidentiality.
- **Authorities,** where we are legally required to disclose, and where lawful we will tell you first.
- **A buyer,** if the business is merged, acquired or sold, with notice to you.

We do not sell personal data. We do not share personal data for cross-context behavioural advertising.

**Sub-processor list.** A current list of our sub-processors is available on request from privacy@zicy.com.

### 11. Where your data goes

Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd. is in Malaysia, and the providers we use operate in several countries, so your data may be processed outside the country you are in.

The Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024 replaced the old transfer whitelist with a risk-based test: a transfer is permitted where the destination has law substantially similar to the PDPA or provides an adequate level of protection, or under one of the Act's other permitted grounds. The Personal Data Protection Commissioner's 2025 Cross-Border Personal Data Transfer Guidelines accept contractual protections, including the European Commission's standard contractual clauses, as one valid way to meet that test.

| Provider | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Google | Firebase Authentication for sign-in, and Google Analytics 4 and Tag Manager for site and product analytics |
| Stripe | Payment processing |
| Sentry | Error and crash monitoring. Sentry's ingest region for Zicy is the United States |
| Vercel | Marketing site hosting and cookieless site analytics |
| OpenAI | Ask Zicy, embeddings, content and analysis features |
| MongoDB Atlas | Primary database and vector search |

You can ask us for more detail on the safeguards at privacy@zicy.com.

### 12. How long we keep things

| Data | Kept for | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Account and profile records | Life of the account, then deleted 90 days after closure | Industry-standard grace period for accidental closure and reactivation |
| Brand profiles, tracked prompts and analysis history | Life of the account, then deleted 90 days after closure | One rule across product data is easier to honour than five |
| AI engine responses | Life of the account, then deleted 90 days after closure | This is the historical trend record the product exists to build |
| Connected Google and Bing data, after disconnect | 30 days | Deliberately short. Google's Limited Use terms push toward prompt deletion, and a short window is a selling point |
| Ask Zicy chat history, after account closure | 90 days | Matches the account rule |
| Generated content drafts | Life of the account, then deleted 90 days after closure | Matches the account rule |
| Billing and invoice records | 7 years | Not discretionary. Malaysian tax law requires business records to be kept for 7 years |
| Security and access logs | 12 months | Long enough for incident forensics, proportionate under storage limitation |
| Data sent to OpenAI | Up to 30 days, held by OpenAI | OpenAI's published API retention for abuse monitoring, then deleted. Not used for training |
| Marketing contacts | Until you unsubscribe, then suppression-list only | |

Data deleted from live systems remains in encrypted backups until the backup cycle overwrites it.

### 13. How we protect it

- Encryption in transit using TLS, and encryption at rest.
- Role-based access control, with staff access limited to those who need it.
- Password hashing, and support for the sign-in methods shown in your account settings.
- Logging and monitoring of access to production systems.
- Contractual security obligations on providers where a data processing agreement is in place.
- Regular review of access rights.

No system is perfectly secure. If a breach occurs that is likely to cause you significant harm, we will notify the Personal Data Protection Commissioner of Malaysia as soon as practicable and in any event within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, and we will notify affected individuals without undue delay and no later than seven days after that report, as required by the Personal Data Protection Act 2010 as amended. Where the GDPR applies, we will meet its equivalent obligations.

### 14. Your rights

**If you are in Malaysia,** under the Personal Data Protection Act 2010, as amended by the Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024, you can: ask for access to the personal data we hold about you; ask us to correct data that is inaccurate, incomplete or out of date; withdraw consent where we rely on it; ask us to stop processing that is causing or likely to cause damage or distress; ask us to stop processing for direct marketing; ask us to transmit your personal data to another data controller, where that is technically feasible and the formats are compatible; complain to the Personal Data Protection Commissioner.

**If you are in the European Economic Area or the United Kingdom,** you can also ask for erasure, restriction of processing, and a copy of your data in a portable format, and you can object to processing based on legitimate interests. You can complain to your local supervisory authority.

**If you are in California,** you can ask what we collect, ask for a copy, ask for deletion, ask for correction, and you have the right not to be discriminated against for exercising these rights. We do not sell personal information and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising, so there is no opt-out for you to exercise on those points.

**How to make a request.** Email privacy@zicy.com. We will verify your identity before acting, and we will respond within the period the law allows, which is 21 days in Malaysia and one month under the GDPR unless we tell you we need longer.

If your data sits inside a Zicy account run by someone else, for example an agency that added you, please contact them first. We will help them respond.

### 15. Children

Zicy is a business tool and is not intended for children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 18. If you believe a child has given us data, email privacy@zicy.com and we will delete it.

### 16. Changes to this policy

We will post any change on this page and update the date at the top. If a change materially affects your rights, we will tell you by email or in the product before it takes effect.

### 17. Contact us

- **Privacy questions and rights requests:** privacy@zicy.com
- **Postal address:** Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd., 60 Persiaran Midlands, 10250 Penang, Malaysia
- **Regulator in Malaysia:** Personal Data Protection Department (Jabatan Perlindungan Data Peribadi), pdp.gov.my
