## Dasar privasi, Zicy

https://www.zicy.com/legal/privacy-bm

Perundangan

Dasar privasi

Kemas kini terakhir: 6 Ogos 2026

Dasar ini diterbitkan dalam Bahasa Inggeris dan Bahasa Malaysia. Sekiranya terdapat percanggahan antara versi Bahasa Malaysia ini dengan versi Bahasa Inggeris, versi Bahasa Inggeris akan diguna pakai.

Dasar ini menerangkan apa yang dikumpul oleh Zicy, sebabnya, dengan siapa kami berkongsi data tersebut, dan apa yang boleh anda minta kami lakukan mengenainya. Zicy dikendalikan oleh Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd. di Penang, Malaysia.

Dasar kuki · Tetapan kuki · English

### 1. Versi ringkas

Ringkasan mudah difahami. Ini hanyalah ringkasan, dan selebihnya dasar ini yang terpakai.

| Soalan | Jawapan |
|---|---|
| Siapa yang menguruskan Zicy | Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd., sebuah syarikat berdaftar di Malaysia. |
| Apa yang kami simpan secara utama | Butiran akaun anda, butiran bil anda, jenama dan prompt yang anda pilih untuk dijejak, dan data yang anda sambungkan daripada Google, Bing dan laman web anda sendiri. |
| Adakah kami menjual data anda | Tidak. Kami tidak menjual data peribadi dan kami tidak berkongsi data tersebut untuk pengiklanan tingkah laku silang konteks (cross-context behavioural advertising). |
| Berapa lama kami menyimpannya | Selagi akaun anda aktif, kemudian untuk tempoh yang dinyatakan dalam seksyen 12. |

### 2. Skop dasar ini

Dasar ini terpakai kepada:

- Aplikasi web Zicy di app.zicy.com
- Laman web pemasaran Zicy di zicy.com dan pusat bantuan di docs.zicy.com
- Sambungan Chrome Zicy
- Alat perunding AEO dan GEO awam di zicy.com/consultant
- Pemalam WordPress Zicy
- Perbualan e-mel, sokongan dan jualan dengan kami

Dasar ini tidak meliputi laman web pihak ketiga yang kami pautkan, atau apa yang dilakukan oleh platform AI dengan soalan yang anda taip terus ke dalamnya.

### 3. Apabila kami menjadi pengawal data dan apabila kami menjadi pemproses data

Perbezaan ini penting jika anda membeli Zicy bagi pihak klien atau majikan anda.

**Kami adalah pengawal data bagi:** butiran akaun dan profil anda; rekod organisasi, pasukan dan jemputan anda; rekod bil, langganan dan kuota; data penggunaan produk, peranti dan log; komunikasi pemasaran dan sokongan.

**Kami adalah pemproses data bagi:** profil jenama, prompt yang dijejak dan senarai pesaing yang anda masukkan; data Analytics dan Search Console yang anda sambungkan; kandungan yang dirayapi daripada laman web yang anda tetapkan; respons enjin AI yang direkodkan bagi prompt yang anda jejak; draf kandungan yang dijana atau dioptimumkan dalam produk.

Bagi kumpulan kedua itu, anda, atau klien yang anda wakili, adalah pengawal data. Terma pemprosesan kami bagi data tersebut boleh diperoleh atas permintaan daripada privacy@zicy.com.

### 4. Apa yang kami kumpul dan sebabnya

Semua yang berikut sama ada diberikan oleh anda, dijana melalui penggunaan Zicy oleh anda, atau diperoleh daripada perkhidmatan yang anda sambungkan.

**4.1 Akaun dan identiti.** Apa: nama penuh, alamat e-mel, kata laluan (disimpan dalam bentuk hash, tidak pernah dalam bentuk boleh baca), nama organisasi, ID organisasi, kaedah log masuk, peranan, skop akses profil. Sebab: untuk mencipta dan melindungi akaun anda, menguatkuasakan kebenaran, dan menyediakan perkhidmatan. Asas undang-undang, apabila GDPR terpakai: pelaksanaan kontrak.

**4.2 Pasukan dan jemputan.** Apa: alamat e-mel, peranan dan status sesiapa yang anda jemput, dan tarikh luput jemputan mereka. Sebab: untuk menguruskan akses pasukan dan peruntukan kuota. Nota: jika anda menjemput rakan sekerja, anda meminta kami menghantar e-mel bagi pihak anda. Jemput hanya orang yang menjangkakan e-mel daripada anda. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak, dan kepentingan sah kami dalam mengendalikan ciri pasukan.

**4.3 Bil dan langganan.** Apa: pelan, penggunaan kuota dan kredit, pembelian tambahan, penebusan baucar, invois, butiran hubungan bil. Sebab: untuk menerima bayaran, mengeluarkan invois, memenuhi kewajipan cukai dan perakaunan. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak, dan kewajipan undang-undang.

**4.4 Data jenama dan prompt.** Apa: nama jenama dan variasinya, URL laman web, industri, produk dan perkhidmatan, misi, cadangan jualan unik, nada dan gaya penulisan, nama dan URL pesaing, fakta jenama seperti tahun penubuhan dan lokasi ibu pejabat, prompt yang anda jejak, dan tag yang anda gunakan. Sebab: setiap modul Zicy ditentukur berdasarkan data ini. Tanpanya kami tidak dapat mengukur apa-apa. Amaran data peribadi: medan ini adalah teks bebas. Jangan masukkan data peribadi tentang individu melainkan perlu, dan jangan sekali-kali masukkan data kategori khas seperti maklumat kesihatan atau biometrik. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak. Jika data tersebut milik klien anda, kami memprosesnya atas arahan anda.

**4.5 Respons enjin AI.** Apa: jawapan yang dikembalikan oleh ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews dan Google AI Mode bagi prompt yang anda jejak, berserta jenama, kedudukan, sentimen dan petikan yang kami ekstrak daripadanya. Cara: kami menghantar prompt yang anda jejak kepada setiap enjin pada kitaran harian dan merekodkan responsnya. Data peribadi sampingan: jawapan AI boleh menyebut nama seseorang, contohnya seorang pengasas atau penulis. Kami menyimpan jawapan tersebut seperti yang dikembalikan supaya anda mempunyai bukti. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak, dan kepentingan sah kami dalam menyediakan rekod pengukuran yang boleh anda percayai.

**4.6 Akaun Google yang disambungkan.** Diliputi secara berasingan dalam seksyen 5, kerana Google mengenakan peraturan khusus ke atas kami.

**4.7 Bing Webmaster Tools yang disambungkan.** Apa: paparan (impressions), klik, kadar klik-tayang, kedudukan purata, halaman teratas dan pertanyaan teratas bagi hartanah yang anda sambungkan. Sebab: indeks Bing turut memberi maklumat kepada Microsoft Copilot dan enjin jawapan lain, jadi ia sebahagian daripada gambaran keterlihatan anda. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak.

**4.8 Pemalam WordPress dan log bot AI.** Apa: rekod log akses yang menunjukkan perayap AI mana yang melawat laman web anda dan halaman mana yang mereka baca. Bergantung pada konfigurasi pelayan anda, log ini boleh mengandungi alamat IP dan rentetan ejen pengguna (user-agent). Sebab: untuk menunjukkan kepada anda pembantu AI mana yang sebenarnya membaca laman web anda dan dari mana mereka mengambil jawapan. Tanggungjawab anda: anda adalah pengawal data bagi log pelayan anda sendiri. Segerakkan log tersebut hanya jika anda berhak berbuat demikian. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak, atas arahan anda.

**4.9 Data rayapan laman web.** Apa: URL halaman, tajuk, meta deskripsi, tajuk kecil, kandungan badan, data berstruktur, robots.txt, peta laman dan llms.txt bagi domain yang anda tetapkan. Sebab: untuk menjalankan audit laman, ringkasan halaman, pengesanan pendua dan penskoran kandungan. Had: kami hanya merayapi domain yang anda tetapkan pada profil jenama, dan kami tidak pernah menerbitkan atau mengubah apa-apa pada laman web anda. Setiap aset yang dihasilkan Zicy diserahkan kepada anda untuk diterbitkan sendiri. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak.

**4.10 Ask Zicy dan perunding AI.** Apa: mesej yang anda taip ke dalam Ask Zicy, tajuk tab sembang yang anda tetapkan, dan respons yang dikembalikan. Sebab: untuk menjawab soalan anda dan mengukur penggunaan sembang berbanding pelan anda. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak.

**4.11 Kandungan yang dijana dan dioptimumkan.** Apa: draf artikel, salinan halaman yang dioptimumkan, penanda skema dan fail llms.txt yang dihasilkan dalam produk, serta input yang anda berikan untuk menghasilkannya. Sebab: supaya pustaka kandungan anda kekal tersimpan dan anda boleh kembali kepada draf. Asas undang-undang: pelaksanaan kontrak.

**4.12 Data penggunaan produk, peranti dan log.** Apa: alamat IP, jenis pelayar dan peranti, halaman dan ciri yang digunakan, cap masa, URL rujukan, rekod ralat dan diagnostik. Sebab: untuk mengekalkan keselamatan perkhidmatan, mendiagnosis kerosakan, mencegah penyalahgunaan, dan memahami ciri yang digunakan. Asas undang-undang: kepentingan sah dalam mengamankan dan menambah baik perkhidmatan.

**4.13 Komunikasi dan pemasaran.** Apa: butiran borang hubungan dan permintaan demo, perbualan sokongan, dan pilihan e-mel. Sebab: untuk membalas anda dan menghantar e-mel produk serta pemasaran yang anda minta. Kawalan: pusat pemberitahuan dalam Settings mempunyai suis induk untuk menjeda semua e-mel pilihan. E-mel mengenai pembayaran, invois dan jemputan adalah operasi dan sentiasa dihantar. Asas undang-undang: persetujuan bagi pemasaran, kepentingan sah bagi mesej operasi.

### 5. Data pengguna Google, dan keperluan Penggunaan Terhad Google

Jika anda menyambungkan Google Analytics atau Google Search Console, Zicy mengakses data pengguna Google melalui API Google, dengan kebenaran jelas anda pada skrin persetujuan.

**Apa yang kami akses:** Google Analytics, metrik trafik, sumber dan penglibatan bagi hartanah yang anda pilih, termasuk sumber rujukan AI yang kami laporkan; Google Search Console, data pertanyaan, paparan, klik, kadar klik-tayang dan kedudukan bagi hartanah yang anda pilih; alamat e-mel akaun Google yang disambungkan, supaya anda dapat melihat akaun mana yang dipautkan dan memutuskan sambungannya.

**Cara kami menggunakannya:** hanya untuk menghasilkan laporan dan ciri yang boleh anda lihat dalam Zicy. Tiada yang lain.

**Komitmen Penggunaan Terhad.** Penggunaan dan pemindahan maklumat oleh Zicy yang diterima daripada API Google mematuhi Google API Services User Data Policy, termasuk keperluan Penggunaan Terhad (Limited Use). Pada dasarnya ini bermaksud: kami menggunakan data pengguna Google hanya untuk menyediakan atau menambah baik ciri yang kelihatan dan menonjol dalam Zicy; kami tidak memindahkan data pengguna Google kecuali untuk menyediakan ciri tersebut dengan persetujuan anda, bagi tujuan keselamatan, untuk mematuhi undang-undang, atau dalam penggabungan, pengambilalihan atau penjualan aset; kami tidak membenarkan manusia membaca data pengguna Google, kecuali apabila anda telah bersetuju secara khusus, apabila perlu bagi keselamatan atau untuk mematuhi undang-undang, atau apabila data tersebut telah diagregatkan bagi operasi dalaman; kami tidak menggunakan data pengguna Google untuk pengiklanan, dan kami tidak menjualnya.

**Cara memutuskan sambungan:** buka Site Traffic dalam aplikasi dan pilih Disconnect pada tab Analytics atau Search Console, atau tarik balik akses Zicy di myaccount.google.com/permissions. Menarik balik akses menghentikan penyegerakan akan datang. Untuk memadam data yang telah diimport, hubungi privacy@zicy.com.

### 6. Sambungan Chrome

Sambungan Chrome Zicy mengaudit sesebuah halaman untuk kesediaan AI apabila anda memintanya.

- Ia menganalisis halaman hanya apabila anda mencetuskan audit. Ia tidak berjalan di latar belakang.
- Ia tidak menjejak atau menghantar sejarah pelayaran anda.
- Ia tidak menjual atau berkongsi data anda dengan pihak ketiga bagi tujuan mereka sendiri.
- Menyahpasang sambungan ini menghentikan semua pengumpulan data.

### 7. Perunding AEO dan GEO awam

Alat perunding di zicy.com/consultant terbuka kepada pelawat tanpa akaun.

- Kami memproses soalan dan URL yang anda hantar bagi tujuan menjawabnya.
- Jangan tampal maklumat sulit atau peribadi ke dalam alat awam.

### 8. Cara kami menggunakan AI, dan sama ada data anda melatih model

Ini soalan yang paling kerap ditanya oleh pembeli, jadi kami menjawabnya secara terus. Kami menggunakan AI dalam dua cara yang berbeza, dan kami memastikan kedua-duanya kekal berasingan, bukan bercampur.

**OpenAI: Ask Zicy, embedding, kandungan dan analisis.** Ask Zicy, embedding kami, serta alat kandungan dan analisis kami berjalan di atas API OpenAI. OpenAI tidak menggunakan data API untuk melatih modelnya melainkan pelanggan bersetuju secara khusus. Zicy tidak bersetuju berbuat demikian. OpenAI boleh menyimpan input dan output API selama sehingga 30 hari bagi tujuan pemantauan penyalahgunaan, kemudian memadamnya. OpenAI telah menamatkan audit SOC 2 Type 2 yang meliputi platform API.

**Prompt yang dijejak dan dihantar kepada enjin AI yang kami ukur.** Secara berasingan daripada cara kami menggunakan OpenAI, Zicy menghantar prompt yang anda jejak kepada ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews dan Google AI Mode, bagi tujuan merekodkan jawapan enjin-enjin tersebut. Itulah produk itu sendiri.

Kami menggunakan statistik yang telah diagregatkan dan dinyahkenal pasti, yang tidak dapat mengenal pasti anda atau klien anda, untuk menambah baik penanda aras dan ciri Zicy. Kami tidak membuat keputusan tentang anda yang mempunyai kesan undang-undang atau kesan ketara yang serupa semata-mata menggunakan pemprosesan automatik.

### 9. Kuki dan teknologi serupa

Kami menggunakan kuki dan teknologi serupa untuk log masuk dan keselamatan, untuk mengingati keutamaan seperti suis tema, dan untuk mengukur penggunaan laman dan produk.

Kuki bukan penting ditetapkan hanya dengan persetujuan anda, dan anda boleh menukar pilihan anda pada bila-bila masa menggunakan Tetapan kuki di bahagian bawah laman. Senarai penuh terdapat dalam dasar kuki.

### 10. Dengan siapa kami berkongsi data

Kami berkongsi data peribadi hanya dengan kategori di bawah, dan hanya sekadar yang diperlukan.

- **Pembekal perkhidmatan, kadangkala digelar sub-pemproses.** Hosting, pangkalan data, penghantaran e-mel, pembayaran, pemantauan ralat, analitik produk dan pembekal AI. Setiap satu terikat dengan syarat penerbitannya sendiri, dan apabila terdapat perjanjian pemprosesan data, perjanjian itu memerlukan pembekal tersebut melindungi data dan memprosesnya hanya atas arahan kami.
- **Enjin AI yang kami ukur.** Kami menghantar teks prompt yang anda jejak.
- **Organisasi anda sendiri.** Sesiapa yang anda jemput boleh melihat profil yang ditugaskan kepada mereka. Pemilik boleh melihat penggunaan dan pembilan organisasi.
- **Penasihat profesional, juruaudit dan penanggung insurans,** tertakluk kepada kerahsiaan.
- **Pihak berkuasa,** apabila kami dikehendaki oleh undang-undang untuk mendedahkan, dan apabila sah kami akan memberitahu anda terlebih dahulu.
- **Pembeli,** jika perniagaan ini digabungkan, diambil alih atau dijual, dengan notis kepada anda.

Kami tidak menjual data peribadi. Kami tidak berkongsi data peribadi untuk pengiklanan tingkah laku silang konteks.

**Senarai sub-pemproses.** Senarai terkini sub-pemproses kami boleh diperoleh atas permintaan daripada privacy@zicy.com.

### 11. Ke mana perginya data anda

Growth Pro Sdn. Bhd. berada di Malaysia, dan pembekal yang kami gunakan beroperasi di beberapa negara, jadi data anda mungkin diproses di luar negara tempat anda berada.

Akta Perlindungan Data Peribadi (Pindaan) 2024 menggantikan rejim senarai putih lama dengan ujian berasaskan risiko: pemindahan dibenarkan apabila destinasi mempunyai undang-undang yang setara secara substansial dengan Akta Perlindungan Data Peribadi atau menyediakan tahap perlindungan yang mencukupi, atau di bawah salah satu asas lain yang dibenarkan oleh Akta tersebut. Garis Panduan Pemindahan Data Peribadi Rentas Sempadan 2025 oleh Pesuruhjaya Perlindungan Data Peribadi menerima perlindungan kontraktual, termasuk klausa kontrak piawai Suruhanjaya Eropah, sebagai satu cara yang sah untuk memenuhi ujian tersebut.

| Pembekal | Tujuan |
|---|---|
| Google | Firebase Authentication untuk log masuk, serta Google Analytics 4 dan Tag Manager untuk analitik laman dan produk |
| Stripe | Pemprosesan pembayaran |
| Sentry | Pemantauan ralat dan kerosakan. Rantau penerimaan Sentry bagi Zicy ialah Amerika Syarikat |
| Vercel | Hosting laman pemasaran dan analitik laman tanpa kuki |
| OpenAI | Ciri Ask Zicy, embedding, kandungan dan analisis |
| MongoDB Atlas | Pangkalan data utama dan carian vektor |

Anda boleh meminta butiran lanjut mengenai perlindungan ini di privacy@zicy.com.

### 12. Berapa lama kami menyimpan data

| Data | Tempoh simpanan | Sebab |
|---|---|---|
| Rekod akaun dan profil | Sepanjang tempoh akaun, kemudian dipadam 90 hari selepas penutupan | Tempoh tangguh piawai industri bagi penutupan tidak sengaja dan pengaktifan semula |
| Profil jenama, prompt yang dijejak dan sejarah analisis | Sepanjang tempoh akaun, kemudian dipadam 90 hari selepas penutupan | Satu peraturan merentasi data produk lebih mudah dipatuhi berbanding lima |
| Respons enjin AI | Sepanjang tempoh akaun, kemudian dipadam 90 hari selepas penutupan | Ini rekod trend sejarah yang menjadi tujuan produk ini dibina |
| Data Google dan Bing yang disambungkan, selepas pemutusan sambungan | 30 hari | Sengaja dipendekkan. Terma Penggunaan Terhad Google menggalakkan pemadaman segera, dan tempoh yang singkat adalah satu titik jualan |
| Sejarah sembang Ask Zicy, selepas penutupan akaun | 90 hari | Selaras dengan peraturan akaun |
| Draf kandungan yang dijana | Sepanjang tempoh akaun, kemudian dipadam 90 hari selepas penutupan | Selaras dengan peraturan akaun |
| Rekod bil dan invois | 7 tahun | Bukan budi bicara. Undang-undang cukai Malaysia mewajibkan rekod perniagaan disimpan selama 7 tahun |
| Log keselamatan dan akses | 12 bulan | Cukup lama untuk forensik insiden, berkadar di bawah prinsip had penyimpanan |
| Data yang dihantar kepada OpenAI | Sehingga 30 hari, disimpan oleh OpenAI | Tempoh simpanan API OpenAI yang diterbitkan bagi pemantauan penyalahgunaan, kemudian dipadam. Tidak digunakan untuk latihan model |
| Kenalan pemasaran | Sehingga anda berhenti melanggan, kemudian hanya senarai sekatan sahaja | |

Data yang dipadam daripada sistem langsung kekal dalam sandaran tersulit sehingga kitaran sandaran menimpanya.

### 13. Cara kami melindunginya

- Penyulitan semasa penghantaran menggunakan TLS, dan penyulitan semasa penyimpanan.
- Kawalan akses berasaskan peranan, dengan akses kakitangan terhad kepada yang memerlukannya sahaja.
- Hashing kata laluan, dan sokongan bagi kaedah log masuk yang dipaparkan dalam tetapan akaun anda.
- Pengelogan dan pemantauan akses kepada sistem produksi.
- Kewajipan keselamatan kontraktual ke atas pembekal yang mempunyai perjanjian pemprosesan data.
- Semakan berkala hak akses.

Tiada sistem yang selamat sepenuhnya. Jika berlaku pelanggaran data yang berkemungkinan menyebabkan kemudaratan ketara kepada anda, kami akan memaklumkan Pesuruhjaya Perlindungan Data Peribadi Malaysia secepat mungkin dan dalam apa jua keadaan dalam masa 72 jam selepas mengetahuinya, dan kami akan memaklumkan individu yang terjejas tanpa kelewatan wajar dan tidak lewat daripada tujuh hari selepas laporan tersebut, sebagaimana dikehendaki oleh Akta Perlindungan Data Peribadi 2010 yang dipinda. Apabila GDPR terpakai, kami akan memenuhi kewajipan setaranya.

### 14. Hak anda

**Jika anda berada di Malaysia,** di bawah Akta Perlindungan Data Peribadi 2010, sebagaimana dipinda oleh Akta Perlindungan Data Peribadi (Pindaan) 2024, anda boleh: meminta akses kepada data peribadi anda yang kami simpan; meminta kami membetulkan data yang tidak tepat, tidak lengkap atau lapuk; menarik balik persetujuan apabila kami bergantung kepadanya; meminta kami menghentikan pemprosesan yang menyebabkan atau berkemungkinan menyebabkan kerosakan atau kesusahan; meminta kami menghentikan pemprosesan bagi pemasaran langsung; meminta kami menghantar data peribadi anda kepada pengawal data lain, apabila itu boleh dilaksanakan secara teknikal dan format serasi; membuat aduan kepada Pesuruhjaya Perlindungan Data Peribadi.

**Jika anda berada di Kawasan Ekonomi Eropah atau United Kingdom,** anda juga boleh meminta pemadaman, sekatan pemprosesan, dan salinan data anda dalam format mudah alih, dan anda boleh membantah pemprosesan yang berasaskan kepentingan sah. Anda boleh membuat aduan kepada pihak berkuasa penyeliaan tempatan anda.

**Jika anda berada di California,** anda boleh bertanya apa yang kami kumpul, meminta salinan, meminta pemadaman, meminta pembetulan, dan anda mempunyai hak untuk tidak didiskriminasi kerana menggunakan hak-hak ini. Kami tidak menjual maklumat peribadi dan kami tidak berkongsinya untuk pengiklanan tingkah laku silang konteks, jadi tiada pilihan keluar untuk anda gunakan pada perkara tersebut.

**Cara membuat permintaan.** E-mel privacy@zicy.com. Kami akan mengesahkan identiti anda sebelum bertindak, dan kami akan membalas dalam tempoh yang dibenarkan oleh undang-undang, iaitu 21 hari di Malaysia dan satu bulan di bawah GDPR melainkan kami memberitahu anda bahawa kami memerlukan masa tambahan.

Jika data anda berada dalam akaun Zicy yang diuruskan oleh pihak lain, contohnya sebuah agensi yang menambah anda, sila hubungi mereka terlebih dahulu. Kami akan membantu mereka membalas.

### 15. Kanak-kanak

Zicy adalah alat perniagaan dan tidak ditujukan untuk kanak-kanak. Kami tidak mengumpul data peribadi daripada sesiapa yang berumur bawah 18 tahun secara sengaja. Jika anda percaya seorang kanak-kanak telah memberikan data kepada kami, e-mel privacy@zicy.com dan kami akan memadamnya.

### 16. Perubahan kepada dasar ini

## Zicy Platform, twelve modules across one loop: measure, diagnose, act, prove

https://www.zicy.com/platform

Platform

The truth layer for AI visibility.

One platform across the whole loop, measure what AI says about your brand, diagnose why, act to fix it, and prove it moved demand. Twelve modules, five engines, built to current AEO/GEO best practice and aligned with Google's latest spam policies. Plain English throughout. No specialist required.

### At a glance

- Zicy is an AI-visibility platform that tracks how AI answer engines mention, cite, and recommend your brand across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Google AI Mode.
- It runs one loop: measure your AI visibility, diagnose where you are losing the answer, act on the gaps, and prove the impact.
- Core metrics include brand mention coverage, citation rate, AI share of voice, and average AI ranking, with the source behind every citation.
- You can see how you stand against named rivals and where the highest-value topics and queries are still open.
- Setup is pasting your website URL; Zicy writes the questions to track.

### 01 · The closed loop

One loop: measure, diagnose, act, prove. The lead module at each stage, the full set is below.

- **01 · Measure — AI Visibility.** The core scoreboard, brand mention coverage, citation rate, AI share of voice and average ranking, per engine, over time.
- **02 · Diagnose — Brand Intelligence.** Perception, the AI Reality Score (fact-check / hallucination), the entity graph, and a prioritised action plan.
- **03 · Act — Action Center.** llms.txt and schema generators, content optimisation, and new citation-ready content.
- **04 · Prove — Site Traffic.** AI-referred sessions and downstream engagement from GA4 and Search Console, connected to the work.

### 02 · The four numbers

Four numbers, every engine, every day. Tracked continuously, reported board-ready.

- **Brand Mention Coverage** — How often your brand is named in the answer.
- **Citation Rate** — How often your brand is explicitly cited or linked.
- **AI Share of Voice** — Your share of category mentions versus tracked rivals.
- **Average AI Ranking** — Where you appear within the answer.

### 03 · The module set

Twelve modules, grouped by loop stage. The whole platform, organised the way the work actually runs.

**Measure**

- **Prompt Manager** — Choose and own the exact questions AI is judged on; build and tag a prompt set across segments, topics and languages, run across all five engines.
- **AI Visibility** — The core scoreboard: brand mention coverage, citation rate, AI share of voice and average ranking, per engine, over time.
- **Competitive AI Performance** — Your standing against named competitors, side by side, on coverage, ranking, citations, share of voice and sentiment.

**Diagnose**

- **Brand Intelligence** — Perception, the AI Reality Score (fact-check / hallucination), the entity graph, and a prioritised action plan.
- **Brand Sentiment** — The language AI attaches to your brand, and the sources driving it.
- **Competitor Sentiment Profiles** — How AI frames each rival, from positive to negative.
- **Key Topics Analysis** — Where you lead the answer, where you are in a fight, and where you are invisible, by topic.
- **Citation Analysis** — Which sources AI cites about you, owned vs. earned vs. competitor vs. uncited, with narrative control and competitor share, down to the URL.
- **Site Audit** — Technical AI-readiness: llms.txt, AI-bot access, schema and page health.
- **Visibility Gaps** — The prioritised list of what to fix and what to publish, ranked by impact.

**Act**

- **Action Center** — The do-it-now toolbox: llms.txt and schema generators, content optimisation, and new citation-ready content.

**Prove**

- **Site Traffic** — AI-referred sessions and downstream engagement from GA4 and Search Console, connected to the visibility work: the line from AI visibility to demand.

In Diagnose, Brand Intelligence surfaces the AI Reality Score.

### 04 · The proof layer

Proof it brought customers, not just mentions.

Does winning the AI answer move demand? Zicy connects AI-referred sessions, answer-intent queries and branded-search behaviour from GA4 and Search Console to the visibility work, so AI visibility stops being a vanity metric. The result is a line that's defensible in a budget review.

Competitors measure. Zicy proves.

The truth layer isn't another metric. It's the fact-check. Zicy flags where AI is wrong about you, not just whether you're mentioned.

- **Truth, not just mentions.** The AI Reality Score catches hallucinations and outdated facts before buyers see them.
- **Every market, every language.** Coverage across the five engines in the languages your customers actually use, wherever they are. Built on Penang-rooted regional strength.

### FAQ

**Q: How many AI engines does Zicy track?**
Zicy tracks five engines by default, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode. Enterprise plans can add others, such as Grok and DeepSeek. Every tracked prompt runs across each engine.

**Q: What is the difference between the loop and the modules?**
The loop (measure, diagnose, act, prove) is the workflow; the modules are the tools that deliver each stage. You move around one loop using twelve modules.

**Q: Does Zicy change my site, or only report on it?**
Zicy both reports and remediates. It measures and diagnoses, then the Action Center generates schema, llms.txt and citation-ready content so you can fix what it finds, without a hand-off to another tool.

**Q: How often does Zicy update?**
Zicy tracks daily on every tier. Answer engines evolve gradually rather than by the hour, but daily tracking means you see meaningful shifts as soon as they happen, not a week after.

Yes. Agencies can run AI visibility under their own brand, with white-label dashboards and deliverables, and manage multiple brands from one place. See the agencies solution page.

## The AI Reality Score, Zicy's per-engine accuracy metric

https://www.zicy.com/platform/ai-reality-score

Zicy · the truth layer

The AI Reality Score

The AI Reality Score is Zicy's per-engine accuracy metric, a score from 0 to 100 measuring how accurately AI engines describe a brand across its tracked prompt set, where 100 means every tracked response was factually correct.

### 01 · Why it exists

A mention is only worth as much as the claim attached to it.

Most AI visibility tools measure presence: was the brand named? The AI Reality Score measures something harder and more important: was what AI said actually true? A brand can appear in nine out of ten AI answers and still be described with an outdated pricing tier, a wrong founding year, or a product feature it discontinued. That inaccuracy reaches the buyer before any page on the brand's website does.

The AI Reality Score exists because a mention is only valuable if the claim attached to it is correct. It is the metric that turns AI visibility from a reach measure into a truth measure, and the number that tells a brand whether its AI visibility work is making AI more accurate, not just more frequent.

### 02 · What it measures

Four signals in every answer.

- **Lifts the score — Accurate descriptions.** AI responses that correctly describe the brand's category, offering, positioning, key facts, and current state. These lift the score.
- **Reduces the score — Outdated claims.** Statements that were once true but are no longer: old pricing, former team members, discontinued products, superseded messaging. These reduce the score.
- **Reduces it most — Hallucinations.** Statements AI asserts about the brand that have no grounding in any published source and were never true. These reduce the score more heavily than outdated claims.
- **Reduces the score — Entity gaps.** Facts the brand should be known for that AI consistently omits: a key product line never mentioned, a market never attributed, a credential never surfaced. These indicate incomplete entity definition and reduce the score.

### 03 · How it is calculated

Scored on what AI says, per engine, over time.

The AI Reality Score is derived from Zicy's structured analysis of actual AI responses across the brand's tracked prompt set on each engine. For each prompt, the AI response is assessed against the brand's known facts: what is stated accurately, what is outdated, what is false, what is missing.

Important: AI-generated responses are probabilistic. The same prompt asked at different times, or phrased slightly differently, can produce different outputs. The AI Reality Score is therefore a directional indicator tracked over time, not a single definitive measurement. Zicy tracks it weekly so changes are meaningful trends, not noise.

A score of 100 means every assessed response across the tracked prompt set was accurate on that engine. Scores below 100 reflect the proportion and severity of inaccuracies found. Scores are per-engine: a brand may score 94 on ChatGPT and 71 on Gemini (illustrative figures), reflecting genuine differences in how each engine has ingested and represented the brand's entity data.

### 04 · What pulls the score down

Inaccuracy, in weight order.

- Hallucinations (highest weight).
- Outdated claims.
- Wrong attributions (features attributed to the wrong product, facts attributed to the wrong team member).
- Missing key facts consistently absent across responses (entity gaps).
- Competitor conflation (AI describing the brand with a competitor's attributes).

### 05 · How to improve it

Give AI clear, correct, corroborated facts.

- **Schema and llms.txt** — Make the brand's correct facts machine-readable and unambiguous. The Action Center in Zicy generates both.
- **Content accuracy** — Publish and maintain clear, crawlable, authoritative content on the facts AI gets wrong. The Content Optimizer identifies which existing pages need updating.
- **Entity gap remediation** — Create content for the topics AI consistently omits. The Visibility Gaps module prioritises these by estimated impact.
- **Source corroboration** — Earn citations from independent sources that state the correct facts. This is the earned-media layer, what AI Citation Enablement is designed to build.

See the modules on the platform, or ask the AEO/GEO consultant what to fix first.

### 06 · How it connects to demand

Accuracy reduces hesitation at the moment of decision.

An accurate AI description reduces buyer hesitation. When AI describes a brand correctly, right category, right differentiators, right proof, the buyer who acts on that answer arrives with correct expectations and higher purchase confidence. Zicy's Site Traffic module connects AI Reality Score improvements to branded-search behaviour and AI-referred sessions over time, the Prove layer of the loop.

### FAQ

**Q: What is the AI Reality Score?**
The AI Reality Score is Zicy's per-engine accuracy metric, a score from 0 to 100 measuring how accurately AI engines describe a brand across its tracked prompt set. It is Zicy's core differentiator: most tools measure whether a brand was named; Zicy also measures whether what was said was true.

**Q: How is the AI Reality Score different from a brand mention score?**
Brand mention coverage tells you how often your brand appeared in AI answers. The AI Reality Score tells you whether those appearances described you correctly. A brand with 90% mention coverage and a Reality Score of 58 is being named frequently but described inaccurately, which may be worse than not being named at all.

**Q: Why does my score differ between engines?**
Each AI engine has ingested different sources, applies different retrieval weights, and updates its knowledge at different rates. Gemini may have indexed a press release that ChatGPT has not. Perplexity may be citing a source with outdated information that the others have deprioritised. Scores differ between engines because the engines themselves differ in what they know about your brand.

**Q: Can I improve my AI Reality Score?**
Yes. The most reliable improvements come from making correct facts machine-readable (schema, llms.txt), publishing and updating accurate content on the specific claims AI gets wrong, filling entity gaps with new content, and building corroborating citations from independent sources. Zicy's Action Center, Content Generator, and Visibility Gaps module are built for exactly this.

**Q: How often is the AI Reality Score recalculated?**
On Starter and Growth plans, Zicy tracks prompts weekly and updates scores accordingly. On Enterprise plans, daily tracking is available. Because AI responses are probabilistic, weekly tracking gives directional trends rather than single-point readings.

**Q: Is a score of 92 out of 100 good?**
It depends on what is pulling it below 100. A score of 92 with one minor outdated claim is a very different situation from a score of 92 with a hallucination that misattributes a product feature. Zicy's Brand Intelligence report breaks down exactly what is reducing the score so the fix can be targeted.

**Q: What counts as a hallucination in Zicy's scoring?**
A hallucination is a specific factual claim AI makes about a brand that has no grounding in any published source and was never true, a wrong founding year, a non-existent product, a team member who never worked there. It is distinct from an outdated claim (which was once true) and from an entity gap (a fact that is missing rather than wrong).

### See your AI Reality Score

Find out whether AI describes your brand accurately, across all five engines.

## What are examples of companies already succeeding with AEO and GEO?

https://www.zicy.com/resources/aeo-geo-examples

Guides

Early AEO and GEO winners are not the biggest publishers but the clearest ones: knowledge-driven firms, consumer innovators and data publishers whose factual, structured, well-sourced content AI can extract and trust. They treat AI visibility as a strategic asset. Zicy measures whether your brand is among those AI cites across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

By Ritu Khanna · 18 April 2026

The era of generative search is no longer theoretical. Some companies are already winning it. Across industries, early adopters of answer engine optimisation and generative engine optimisation are seeing their brands mentioned, cited and recommended by AI platforms such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. What is notable is that many did not set out to optimise for AI specifically; their focus on clarity, structure and credibility naturally aligns with how AI systems retrieve and rank information.

### Who wins: Which types of companies see early success.

The common denominator among early winners is that they treat AI visibility as an asset, not an experiment. They tend to fall into three groups:

- **Knowledge-driven organisations:** consulting firms, analytics platforms and SaaS companies that publish structured insights. Their content is factual, well-cited and entity-rich, ideal for AI extraction.
- **Consumer-facing innovators:** health, travel and fintech companies that translate expertise into concise, schema-backed content, and dominate when AI answers which is best, how to choose, or what is safe.
- **Media and data publishers:** outlets that maintain accurate, regularly updated data sets such as product reviews, research summaries and comparison charts, which generative engines lean on.

They also focus on high-intent query spaces, where users are actively seeking guidance, comparisons or recommendations, making them more likely to be cited. Each demonstrates the same principle: clarity and verifiability outperform volume and hype. This overlaps with which industries generative search affects most.

### What they do: What they do differently from traditional SEO leaders.

Instead of chasing rankings, successful brands focus on structuring knowledge, through three shifts AI engines recognise:

- **Entity-first publishing:** they define key entities, company, products and experts, using schema markup and Wikidata. See which schema and entity markup matter most.
- **Answer-centric formatting:** their pages read like explanations, not sales copy, so AI can extract concise, factual segments.
- **Source-credibility layering:** they back every claim with references, internal cross-links and external validation. See how to build trust signals AI recognises.

The result is that they become the default mentions in AI conversations, the names users see quoted for their category. They optimise for extractability, keeping key insights in concise, self-contained sections, and they build topic-level authority, where multiple pieces reinforce expertise within a domain rather than relying on isolated high-performing pages.

### Results: What measurable results they achieve.

Although AI citation analytics are still emerging, these brands report tangible advantages: increased brand recall, since users recognise their name from AI summaries even without a click; higher conversion intent, since leads from AI-referred exposure show stronger trust and shorter decision cycles; and cross-platform authority, since once cited in one engine, they are often re-quoted across others. In short, they are not just visible, they are believed, and repeated citations across platforms build category dominance, where a brand becomes strongly associated with specific topics. You can see real case studies on the Zicy case studies page.

### Lessons: What other brands can learn.

The takeaway is clear: AI does not reward scale, it rewards structure. Brands succeeding with AEO and GEO are not publishing more, they are publishing smarter, with clarity, credibility and context designed for both humans and machines. Prioritise quality of information over quantity of content, focusing on accuracy, completeness and relevance, and align content, entity signals and trust signals so every layer reinforces the same narrative. In the generative era, visibility is earned not by shouting the loudest but by being the clearest voice in the data, and success is less about tactics than about building a system of clarity, trust and consistency that AI engines can repeatedly rely on.

## How will Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT change SEO for your business?

https://www.zicy.com/resources/ai-overviews-chatgpt-seo

Guides

Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT are moving discovery from ranked links to synthesised answers, so SEO shifts from ranking to being cited in a limited answer set. Clarity, entity accuracy and cross-platform consistency matter more than domain size, and traffic may flatten while influence rises. Zicy measures whether AI cites you across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

By Ritu Khanna · 16 April 2026

With Google AI Overviews and conversational tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity and Copilot, users now receive synthesised answers instead of traditional search results. For businesses this is a profound shift: SEO is no longer just about ranking, it is about being referenced in AI-generated answers. As AI answer layers become the default interface for many informational queries, especially in research-heavy and B2B categories, brands compete not for page position but for inclusion within a compressed answer set. Understanding how that affects visibility, traffic and conversions belongs in every brand's plan.

### The shift: What is really changing in how people find information.

Traditional search relies on link lists, and users click to learn more. AI-powered search delivers answers directly, often summarising insights from multiple trusted sources. That means fewer clicks but more influence concentrated in the limited set of sources AI cites. AI Overviews reduce the visibility gap between top-ranking and mid-ranking pages: what matters now is content clarity and credibility, not just keyword dominance. ChatGPT, for example, may quote a smaller blog if it gives a cleaner, fact-based explanation that matches intent better than a top-ranked corporate page. Ranking is no longer a proxy for AI visibility: engines prioritise extractability and confidence over domain size, so smaller but well-structured sources can outperform larger sites.

AI engines also evolve dynamically. They do not just crawl websites, they learn from aggregated behaviour, authority and consistency across contexts, so your digital footprint, including articles, social bios, Wikidata entries and structured facts, now acts as your true ranking signal. When the same fact appears consistently across platforms, it is more likely to be cited, effectively making multi-platform consistency a ranking signal in the AI layer. See what content AI prefers to cite and how PR and Wikidata improve AI visibility.

### For SEO teams: What this means for businesses already investing in SEO.

It does not make SEO obsolete, it transforms it. Instead of optimising for algorithms, you now optimise for interpretation, focusing on:

- **Answerability:** can your pages directly and concisely answer high-intent questions?
- **Entity clarity:** are your products, services and expertise recognised as distinct and authoritative by AI models?
- **Consistency across channels:** do your brand facts match across your site, press mentions and social profiles?

The new SEO is about teaching AI how to represent your brand, and that starts with answer engine optimisation and generative engine optimisation. Your analytics will change too. Expect organic traffic to flatten or decline, not because visibility dropped but because more users get their answers before they click. This is where the ROI of being cited matters: being cited still drives awareness and trust without the visit. Attribution shifts from last-click to pre-click influence, where AI mentions contribute to branded searches, direct visits and assisted conversions, and AI-driven discovery often shortens the consideration cycle, improving conversion quality even as total traffic declines.

### How to adapt: How companies should adapt their SEO strategies now.

Forward-thinking teams are shifting priorities from ranking pages to earning citations:

- **Audit for AI accessibility:** ensure robots.txt, sitemap and schema markup are open and descriptive.
- **Invest in brand-authority assets:** author pages, expert credentials, verified data and a consistent tone all boost credibility.
- **Track citation metrics:** monitor AI responses that mention your domain or products. See how to track AI citations and their impact.

SEO is not dead, it is evolving into semantic visibility management: being the trusted source behind the answer, not just one of the links beneath it. Rethink content design at the section level, so each section addresses a single intent, gives a complete, self-contained explanation, and avoids depending on surrounding context. Technical accessibility for AI crawlers is critical too, since blocking or limiting AI bots, intentionally or via infrastructure defaults, can significantly reduce your chances of being included, as covered in Cloudflare bot management for AI discoverability. Businesses that evolve from optimising for rankings to optimising for relevance, structure and authority will hold tomorrow's digital attention.

### See whether AI answers include you

Zicy tracks your citations and mentions across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

## Can AI engines like Copilot or Gemini recommend your products to users?

https://www.zicy.com/resources/ai-product-recommendations

Guides

Yes. AI assistants increasingly recommend specific products, not just answer questions. Whether yours is recommended depends on structured, complete product data and brand authority AI can trust, more than on ads or rankings. Zicy measures where AI names and cites your brand across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

By Ritu Khanna · 17 April 2026

AI assistants are evolving from answering questions to suggesting solutions, including specific products, services and brands. When users ask which laptop is best for graphic design, or what the safest sunscreen is for sensitive skin, engines can surface curated product suggestions, and shopping-focused assistants such as Microsoft Copilot and Gemini increasingly do this directly. For businesses, the next wave of ecommerce visibility will come less from ads or rankings and more from AI recommendations powered by structured, trusted data. This is a shift from search-driven discovery to guided decision-making, where AI filters options into a shortlist, often reducing how many brands a user evaluates. It is a specialised case of answer engine optimisation.

### Selection: How AI engines choose which products to recommend.

AI engines do not browse your website like humans; they synthesise from knowledge graphs, verified data and product feeds. Their recommendation logic depends on:

- **Structured product data:** detailed specifications, schema markup and accurate metadata such as price, category and reviews.
- **Brand authority:** the reputation and consistency of your brand across the web.
- **User context:** the AI interprets the query, its intent, location or preference, and matches it with high-confidence product data.

The more machine-readable and verifiable your product information is, the more likely it is to appear in AI-generated lists. Attribute completeness matters, since products with clearly defined features are easier to match to intent, as does comparability, since products easily compared across standard attributes are more likely to appear in best-of or top-options lists. Much of this depends on preparing your site for Google AI Overviews.

Buyers now ask AI for the shortlist, and they act on it.

- 55% of AI users research products with AI weekly, using it to narrow choices (57%) and compare options (53%) (Semrush, 1,030 US consumers, 2025).
- 50% have bought something after AI research, and 22% completed a purchase inside an AI tool (Semrush, 2025).
- But 86% still verify a recommendation before buying, mostly on Google and brand sites (Semrush, 2025).

AI narrows the field; being on the shortlist is what matters.

### Authority: Why brand authority matters as much as data accuracy.

Even when product data is available, AI engines prefer citing trusted brands. Authority acts as a multiplier: two identical data entries can produce different outcomes if one brand is considered more reliable. That reliability is signalled through mentions and citations across credible sites, authoritative entity recognition within AI models, and reinforced reputation via news, encyclopaedias or external validation. This is where AEO and GEO intersect with product visibility: you are not just optimising SKUs, you are teaching AI to associate your brand with trust, relevance and category leadership. AI often applies a confidence threshold when recommending, and stronger authority signals help a brand pass it, especially for high-consideration queries, while repeated inclusion builds a category-association effect. See how to become an authoritative entity for AI engines.

Recommendations are built from third-party signals, not your product page.

- For product-category questions, best-of listicles account for about 44% of ChatGPT's citations, against 14% for standard blog posts (Ahrefs, 75,000 brands, 2025).
- Reddit, Wikipedia and Amazon are among ChatGPT's most-cited domains, so reviews, community and marketplace presence shape which products it names (Ahrefs, 2025).
- More than 60% of consumers report high trust in AI results, and for daily users AI is now the single most influential purchase touchpoint (BCG, 9,000+ respondents per wave, 2025).

### Ethically: Can brands influence AI recommendations ethically?

Yes, through transparent optimisation, not manipulation. The brands that succeed treat AI as a distribution channel for verified expertise, not just product promotion. Key strategies:

- Publish neutral, factual product comparisons that position your brand as an educator, not just a seller.
- Keep website data, merchant feeds and structured product markup consistent.
- Ensure real user reviews and quality ratings are indexed by AI engines.
- Use AEO-aligned metadata to connect products to broader topics.

Optimise for use-case queries such as for beginners, for sensitive skin or for small businesses, since AI frequently maps intent to scenarios rather than generic categories, and create decision-support content that explains how to choose, compare or evaluate products, which AI often uses as the basis for a recommendation. Done well, this helps AI recommend your products organically, the digital equivalent of word of mouth. The prompts you track should reflect these buying-intent queries.

Two guardrails to plan around.

- Recommendations diverge by engine: only about 11% of domains cited by ChatGPT are also cited by Perplexity (The Digital Bloom, 680 million citations, 2025), so you earn each engine separately.
- Manufacturing recommendations is against the rules: since 15 May 2026 Google treats inauthentic brand mentions used to manipulate AI answers as spam (Search Engine Land, 2026).

The ethical path is the durable one: accurate product data, genuine reviews and earned coverage, the Authority pillar in Growth.pro's PAVA framework.

### Long term: The long-term opportunity for brands.

As AI assistants integrate shopping, they will act as personalised decision advisors. That means fewer clicks but stronger brand recall for those cited or recommended, and in time AI-driven recommendations could rival ad placements in influence without the cost. The brands that win will blend data integrity, content clarity and ethical transparency, because the AI marketplace rewards truth more than hype. This may redefine digital shelf space: instead of competing for page positions, brands compete for placement within AI-generated shortlists, where only a limited number of products are surfaced per query, and as personalisation improves, rich, contextual product data that adapts to different user scenarios becomes critical. AI does not sell products, it recommends trust, so the goal is not just to be listed but to be chosen, by both algorithms and the audiences they serve. It connects back to the ROI of being cited by AI engines.

### FAQ

**Q: How do I get my product recommended by ChatGPT when buyers ask for the best option?**
Earn presence in the sources AI reads for recommendations. Best-of listicles supply about 44% of ChatGPT's product-category citations (Ahrefs, 75,000 brands, 2025), so accurate product data plus genuine reviews and third-party coverage matter more than your own page.

**Q: Why does AI recommend competitors instead of my product?**
Because rivals have stronger third-party signals in the sources that engine trusts. Recommendations also diverge by engine, with only about 11% of domains shared between ChatGPT and Perplexity (The Digital Bloom, 680 million citations, 2025), so a competitor can lead one engine and not another.

**Q: Do reviews on G2, Amazon and Reddit affect whether AI recommends my product?**
Yes. Reddit, Wikipedia and Amazon are among ChatGPT's most-cited domains (Ahrefs, 2025), so genuine reviews, marketplace presence and community discussion feed the recommendation.

**Q: Why do ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini recommend different products for the same question?**
They draw on different source pools, so their shortlists differ. You have to earn visibility on each engine rather than assuming one placement carries across all of them.

### See whether AI recommends you, or a competitor

Zicy measures how AI names, cites and recommends your brand across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

## What new KPIs replace traditional SEO metrics in the age of AI search?

https://www.zicy.com/resources/ai-search-kpis

Guides

In AI search, click-based SEO metrics no longer capture performance. The new KPIs measure influence at the answer level: AI citation volume, brand mention share, entity accuracy, positioning within answers, and citation-to-lead correlation. Zicy tracks these across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode, turning zero-click AI visibility into a measurable signal.

By Ritu Khanna · 21 April 2026

For years, marketers measured SEO success through rankings, traffic and conversions. But with Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity shaping how users get answers, those metrics no longer tell the full story. Visibility is no longer about clicks. It is about citations, mentions and share of conversation, which calls for a new set of KPIs. This is the transition from performance visibility, what users click, to perception visibility, what users believe based on AI answers, a fundamentally different measurement paradigm. It builds directly on answer engine optimisation.

### The gap: Why traditional SEO metrics are no longer enough.

Search results have evolved from lists of links to direct answers, which introduces three challenges:

- **Zero-click behaviour:** users often get what they need from AI answers without visiting your site.
- **Opaque attribution:** you may influence buyer decisions without seeing traffic spikes in analytics.
- **AI-mediated discovery:** visibility now depends on whether AI systems reference you, not whether Google ranks you.

Click-through rate and keyword rankings alone can no longer measure success. Traditional metrics operate at the page level, while AI visibility operates at the answer or snippet level, so high-ranking pages may still have low AI visibility. AI visibility needs metrics that measure influence, authority and representation even when clicks do not occur.

The old scoreboard is going dark.

- With an AI summary present, users click a result in only 8% of searches, against 15% without one, and just 1% click a link inside the summary (Pew Research Center, 900 US adults, 2025).
- Ranking is decoupling from citation: only 38% of AI Overview citations now come from the top 10 results, down from 76% a year earlier (Ahrefs, 863,000 keywords, 2026).
- Visibility is volatile: a brand can appear in 86% of tracked answers one period and 14% the next (Similarweb, 2025).

Rankings, clicks and impressions still exist, but they no longer describe how buyers find you.

### New KPIs: The KPIs that define AEO and GEO performance.

The next-generation measurement stack for AI-era visibility includes:

- **AI citation volume:** how often your domain or brand is cited in AI answers, the new organic impression. See how to track AI citations and their impact.
- **Brand mention share, or share of voice:** how often your brand appears in generative responses versus competitors, a proxy for authority in your niche.
- **Entity accuracy:** how consistently AI engines represent your brand facts, such as industry, services and location.
- **Answer influence, weighted by prominence:** your content's visibility in AI outputs, giving more weight to a top answer than a supporting mention.
- **Citation-to-lead correlation:** how AI-driven exposure aligns with inbound inquiries or signups, the bridge between awareness and revenue.

Many teams also add prompt coverage rate, average AI positioning within answers, and citation consistency across repeated prompts over time. Collectively these shift focus from traffic to trust-based influence, measuring how your brand shapes digital conversations rather than just appearing in them.

Measure presence in the answer, not position in a list. The metrics that matter now:

- Mention coverage: the share of tracked prompts that name you.
- Citation rate: the share that link you as a source.
- AI share of voice: your mentions against the competitor set.
- Average AI ranking: where you appear when named.
- AI-referred traffic and its conversion: the downstream signal.

Google is catching up: Search Console added generative AI performance reports in June 2026, though it still reports impressions more clearly than clicks (Google Search Console, 2026).

### Reporting: How to report AI visibility to leadership.

For executives and boards, the challenge is not data but clarity. To communicate AEO and GEO performance, combine qualitative and quantitative insights, pairing citation metrics with narrative context such as the specific summaries your brand is now referenced in. Visualise longitudinal growth to show how citations compound even when click volume plateaus, and align AI KPIs with the traditional funnel by mapping AI-driven awareness to trust to lead conversion. Many teams combine several KPIs into a single composite visibility index that is easy for executives to read. Reframing reports around influence and brand equity shows that AEO is not replacing SEO but evolving it. The guide on presenting AEO and GEO performance in C-suite reports goes further.

### Outcomes: How these KPIs connect to business outcomes.

Unlike traditional SEO, which rewards visibility through position, AEO rewards visibility through credibility. When AI engines repeatedly mention or cite your brand, they effectively become advocates for your expertise, which over time improves lead trust and conversion efficiency, perceived market leadership, and lower dependency on paid reach. AI visibility also supports demand generation efficiency, since users exposed to trusted recommendations convert with less friction, and brands with strong AI presence tend to see higher-quality inbound leads that arrive with pre-established trust. Tracking these KPIs helps teams quantify intangible assets, reputation, recall and influence, that now drive commercial value. SEO used to measure visibility through clicks; AEO measures authority through citations, and the brands that track both see not just traffic but trust at scale.

These map to money because AI-referred visitors behave better. They stayed 41% longer, viewed 12% more pages and bounced 23% less than other visitors, and their conversion gap narrowed from 43% below other traffic to just 9% in seven months (Adobe Analytics, 2025).

Measure it continuously and honestly. Manufacturing mentions is now treated as spam (Search Engine Land, 2026), and citations shift day to day, so trends beat snapshots. This is the measurement layer of Growth.pro's PAVA framework.

### FAQ

**Q: What metrics should replace keyword rankings for measuring AI search?**
Track presence in the answer, not position in a list: mention coverage, citation rate, AI share of voice, average AI ranking, and AI-referred traffic with its conversion. These describe whether AI names, cites and recommends you, which rankings no longer predict (Ahrefs, 863,000 keywords, 2026).

**Q: Why does my brand appear in AI answers one day and vanish the next?**
Because AI citations are volatile. A brand can appear in 86% of tracked answers one period and 14% the next (Similarweb, 2025). Measure continuously across a fixed prompt set and read the trend, not a single snapshot.

**Q: Does AI referral traffic actually convert?**
Increasingly, yes. AI-referred visitors stayed 41% longer and viewed 12% more pages, and their conversion gap versus other traffic narrowed from 43% to just 9% in seven months (Adobe Analytics, 2025). Measure your own cohorts to confirm.

**Q: Can Google Search Console show my AI search performance?**
Partly. Search Console added generative AI performance reports in June 2026, breaking out impressions for AI Overviews and AI Mode, though clicks are still bundled into the main report (Google Search Console, 2026).

### Measure influence, not just clicks

Zicy reports AI citations, mention share, positioning and entity accuracy across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

## How can you build digital trust signals that AI engines recognise?

https://www.zicy.com/resources/ai-trust-signals

Guides

Trust signals are the machine-readable cues, verified authorship, transparent sources, consistent facts and secure infrastructure, that tell AI a brand is real, reliable and worth citing. AI evaluates them continuously through verifiability, consistency and completeness. Zicy tracks whether that credibility is translating into AI visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

By Ritu Khanna · 18 April 2026

Trust has always been a cornerstone of marketing, but now it needs to be machine-readable. As platforms like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity shape how people discover brands, credibility is not judged by human perception alone. AI engines analyse thousands of trust signals, the digital cues that tell them your brand is real, reliable and worth citing. In the AI era those signals function as validation inputs: structured evidence that helps models decide whether your content can be safely included in generated answers. This is closely tied to answer engine optimisation.

### Definition: What trust signals mean in the AI era.

On the traditional web, trust came from backlinks and reviews. On the AI-driven web, trust is built through verifiable transparency: facts, context and reputation that machines can cross-check. AI engines ask three silent questions when evaluating your site:

- Can I verify this information across multiple credible sources?
- Is the author or organisation recognised elsewhere online?
- Is this information current, clear and complete?

If your digital presence answers yes to all three, you are feeding AI the same confidence humans feel when dealing with a known brand. These signals are evaluated continuously, so trust is not a one-time achievement but a dynamic state maintained over time. AI also assesses consistency: stable, repeated signals strengthen trust, while conflicting or outdated information weakens it. Trust signals are the verification layer beneath becoming an authoritative entity.

### What matters: Which trust signals matter most.

AI engines prioritise signals that demonstrate factual accuracy, consistency and authority. The most influential include:

- **Verified authorship:** associate real experts with every piece of content, with bios, credentials and profile links.
- **Transparent sources:** reference data, research or case studies that can be independently validated.
- **Updated content:** AI favours recent, revised information, since freshness implies reliability.
- **Secure infrastructure:** HTTPS, structured metadata and accessible sitemaps confirm technical trustworthiness.
- **Cross-platform consistency:** brand details such as name, tagline, services and leadership must match across your website, press coverage and business directories.

Not all signals carry equal weight. Those tied to verifiability, sources, authorship and external validation, tend to have a stronger impact than purely technical ones, and signal alignment, where multiple signals reinforce the same narrative, increases AI confidence in your credibility. Being consistently cited is one measurable outcome, so pair this with citation coverage tracking.

AI trusts what it can verify and what others confirm, not what you claim.

- Earned beats owned: about 84% of AI citations come from third-party media, and just 0.3% from paid or advertorial (Muck Rack, 25M+ links, 2026).
- Reviews are a trust signal: 34.5% of Google AI Overviews cite a review platform, rising to 49% when the query asks for reviews, and five platforms supply 88% of those citations (SE Ranking, 30,000 keywords, 2026).
- On G2, 80% of products now get more AI citations than human pageviews (G2, 80,000+ products, 2026).

Presence on the sources AI already trusts is itself a trust signal.

### How to: How brands can actively enhance these signals.

Building trust is not about perfection but coherence. To translate human credibility into machine-interpretable proof:

- **Standardise brand data:** use the same factual descriptors, founded date, CEO name, HQ city, everywhere online.
- **Show expertise:** publish authored explainers, whitepapers and guides that address core industry queries.
- **Integrate transparency layers:** add schema markup for reviews, FAQs and authorship.
- **Strengthen external validation:** earn citations from credible domains such as universities, news outlets or verified directories.

Refresh trust signals regularly rather than leaving them static, and build interlinked trust ecosystems where your content references and is referenced by other credible entities. These actions help AI models connect your digital presence to a consistent identity, reinforcing your trust graph over time. When you are ready to test the outcome, see how to get cited in ChatGPT and Perplexity.

Build signals AI can read and corroborate:

1. Put named authors and real expertise on your pages; demonstrated expertise carries to AI surfaces (Google Search Central, 2026).
2. Cite sources and add original data; each of citations, quotations and statistics lifted AI visibility by about 30% to 40% in a controlled study (Princeton GEO study, 10,000 queries, 2024).
3. Earn coverage across many independent sources; only 2.7% of cited domains appear on all five engines, so breadth is what makes you durable (SurfacedBy, 127,198 citations, 2026).
4. Keep your entity data consistent across the web so AI recognises you.

### Advantage: Why trust signals are the new competitive advantage.

In generative search, AI models curate answers rather than ads, so you cannot pay for placement. You must earn your spot through reliability. The brands that win are those AI systems repeatedly cite because they have proven integrity, clarity and authority in their digital footprint. This creates an environment where brands with stronger trust signals gain disproportionate visibility, since AI prefers a smaller set of highly reliable sources over a large set of uncertain ones, and as AI evolves, trust signals will increasingly influence not just citations but recommendations, comparisons and decision-making outputs. AI engines reward brands that are verifiable, transparent and consistent. Digital trust signals are not decoration; they are the currency of credibility in the generative web, and brands that build and maintain them benefit from compounding credibility as AI continues to reuse trusted sources.

This is now the only safe game. Since 15 May 2026 Google treats bought or faked citations as spam, enforced through its June 2026 update (Search Engine Land, 2026), and recovery takes months. Earned, corroborated trust is the durable moat, the Authority pillar in Growth.pro's PAVA framework.

### FAQ

**Q: What trust signals do AI engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity actually look for?**
Verifiable, corroborated ones: named authors and expertise, cited sources and original data, earned third-party coverage, and consistent entity data. About 84% of AI citations come from third-party media rather than owned pages (Muck Rack, 25M+ links, 2026).

**Q: Do author bios and named experts (E-E-A-T) help you get cited by AI?**
They help. Google states that optimising for AI search is optimising for the search experience, where demonstrated expertise matters (Google Search Central, 2026). Named authors, credentials and cited sources make your expertise verifiable to both readers and AI.

**Q: Do online reviews on G2 or Reddit affect whether AI recommends my brand?**
Yes, materially. 34.5% of Google AI Overviews cite a review platform (SE Ranking, 30,000 keywords, 2026), and on G2 most products now get more AI citations than human pageviews (G2, 80,000+ products, 2026). Genuine reviews and community presence feed AI trust.

**Q: Is earned media or my own website more likely to be cited by AI?**
Earned media, by a wide margin, at about 84% of AI citations versus a small share for owned sites (Muck Rack, 25M+ links, 2026). Your site still matters for accuracy, but independent coverage does most of the citing.

### See whether your credibility is earning citations

Zicy tracks how AI describes and cites your brand across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

## What does it mean to become an authoritative entity for AI engines?

https://www.zicy.com/resources/authoritative-entity

Guides

An authoritative entity is a brand that AI engines recognise as a uniquely identifiable, verified part of the knowledge graph, not just a set of pages. Authority shifts from backlinks to consistent, corroborated facts about who you are. Zicy tracks how accurately AI describes your entity, and your AI visibility, across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.

By Ritu Khanna · 18 April 2026

In traditional SEO, authority meant backlinks and domain strength. In the AI era, authority means something deeper: being understood and trusted as a factual entity. When systems like ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity cite your brand as a reliable source, they are not responding to keywords but to credibility patterns. Becoming an authoritative entity means your organisation is formally recognised by machines as a verified part of the global knowledge graph. This is a move from document-level authority, pages and links, to entity-level authority, who you are rather than just what you publish, a more persistent and scalable form of visibility, and it is a core part of answer engine optimisation.

### Definition: What an authoritative entity is.

In AI and semantic search, an entity is a uniquely identifiable object, a company, person, product or concept, that algorithms can connect across multiple data sources. When your brand is structured as an entity, AI engines can distinguish you from competitors, understand your expertise and recall you across topics. Being authoritative means that recognition is reinforced by trustworthy evidence: consistent facts, verified authorship and external validation. Strong entity definition supports disambiguation, so AI systems identify your brand correctly even when similar names exist, and well-defined entities are retrieved across more query variations. In simple terms, SEO tells search engines what you do; AEO teaches AI who you are and why you are credible.

### Trust: How AI engines decide which entities to trust.

AI systems use contextual correlation and credibility scoring, cross-referencing your brand information with data from multiple authoritative sources. Trust builds when your brand facts, name, description, founders, sector and location, are consistent across your website, profiles such as LinkedIn, Crunchbase and Wikidata, news mentions and PR coverage, and structured data markup.

When these align, AI models form a single, stable understanding of your entity. Consensus signals matter: when multiple independent sources confirm the same information, confidence increases significantly. Contextual relevance matters too, since consistent association with specific topics reinforces your authority within those domains. Much of this depends on the schema you publish, covered in which schema and entity markup matter most.

### How to: How a brand strengthens its entity authority.

To be recognised as authoritative, a brand builds a rounded evidence profile that reinforces its credibility from every angle:

- **Consistency:** all external references use the same company name, tagline and core description.
- **Clarity:** schema markup defines organisation type, founders, headquarters and services.
- **Authorship:** real experts are associated with the brand through bylines and verified credentials.
- **Cross-validation:** your entity links to other trusted entities such as partners, certifications and awards.

Brands should also build topic-entity alignment, reinforcing expertise within a defined set of topics rather than spreading across unrelated areas, and establish first-party authority signals such as original research or proprietary data, which AI systems are more likely to reference. Over time these efforts create a stronger entity footprint, increasing the likelihood of being cited across queries. The companion guide on building trust signals AI recognises covers the verification layer in detail.

### Why now: Why this matters now.

As AI-generated results replace traditional search, engines rely more on entities than URLs, so your entity authority determines your visibility. The stronger your profile, the more likely AI engines are to cite you across queries, even outside your direct niche. This creates a threshold effect: brands below a certain level of entity authority may rarely be cited, while those above it gain consistent visibility across multiple use cases. Being recognised as an authoritative entity increasingly becomes the entry ticket to being mentioned, recommended or quoted in AI-generated experiences, from summaries to product recommendations. Becoming an authoritative entity is not about gaming algorithms but earning digital trust through verifiable truth, and brands that invest in a strong, consistent entity today benefit from long-term, compounding visibility. In the AI-driven internet, authority is not claimed. It is confirmed.

### See how AI recognises your brand as an entity

Zicy measures how accurately, and how often, AI describes your brand across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode.
